text: EX-10.2 3 ex102conformed.htm EX-10.2 ex102conformed 1 NON-QUALIFIED SHARE OPTION AGREEMENT THIS AGREEMENT (this “Agreement”), dated November 20, 2026 (the “Grant Date”), is made by and between Tanger Inc. (formerly Tanger Factory Outlet Centers, Inc.), a North Carolina corporation, hereinafter referred to as the “Company”, Tanger Properties Limited Partnership, a North Carolina partnership, hereinafter referred to as the “Partnership”, and Stephen Yalof, an employee of the Partnership, hereinafter referred to as the “Optionee”; WHEREAS, the Company wishes to afford the Optionee the opportunity to purchase its Common Shares; WHEREAS, the Company wishes to carry out the Incentive Award Plan of Tanger Inc. and Tanger Properties Limited Partnership (Amended and Restated as of May 19, 2023) (the “Plan”); and WHEREAS, the Committee, appointed to administer the Plan, has determined that it would be to the advantage and best interest of the Company and its shareholders to grant the Non-Qualified Share Option provided for herein to the Optionee as an inducement to enter into or remain in the service of the Partnership and as an incentive for increased efforts during such service, and has advised the Company thereof and instructed the undersigned officers to issue said Option; NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants herein contained and other good and valuable consideration, receipt of which is hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto do hereby agree as follows: ARTICLE I RELATION TO PLAN This Award is made pursuant to the Plan, all the terms of which are hereby incorporated by reference and made a part of this Agreement. In the event of any conflict between the terms of the Plan and the terms of this Agreement, the terms of the Plan shall govern. Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed thereto in the Plan. ARTICLE II GRANT OF OPTION Section 2.1. Grant of Option On the Grant Date and in consideration of the Optionee’s agreement to remain in the employ of the Company and the Partnership and for other good and valuable consideration, the Company irrevocably grants to the Optionee an option to purchase any part or all of an aggregate of 1,000,000 Common Shares (the “Option”) upon the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement. Section 2.2. Purchase Price The purchase price of the Common Shares covered by the Option shall be $46.20 per share without commission or other charge, which is equal to or greater than the Fair Market Value per Common Share on the Grant Date. Exhibit 10.2 2 Section 2.3. Consideration to Company In consideration of the granting of the Option by the Company, the Optionee agrees to render faithful and efficient services to the Company and the Partnership. Nothing in this Agreement or in the Plan shall confer upon the Optionee any right to continue in the employ of the Company and/or Partnership or shall interfere with or restrict in any way the rights of the Company and the Partnership, which are hereby expressly reserved, to discharge the Optionee at any time for any reason whatsoever, with or without cause, except to the extent expressly provided otherwise in a written agreement between the Partnership, the Company and Optionee. Section 2.4. Adjustments in Option The Optionee acknowledges and agrees that, notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, the Option is subject to adjustment, modification and termination in certain events as provided in Section 11.3 of the Plan. ARTICLE III PERIOD OF EXERCISABILITY Section 3.1. Vesting Generally. The Option will become exercisable in full on December 31, 2030 if: (a) the Optionee has remained continuously employed by the Company and the Partnership through and including December 31, 2030; (b) a Change in Control did not occur prior to the fourth anniversary of the Grant Date; and (c) the arithmetic mean of the Fair Market Value of a Common Share for the twenty (20) consecutive Trading Days ending on (and including) the date that is 48 months immediately following the Grant Date (or if the fourth anniversary of the Grant Date is not a Trading Day, then the last Trading Day preceding the fourth anniversary of the Grant Date) (such date, the “Vesting Target Date”) equals or exceeds $61.20 (the “Vesting Trigger Price”). For purposes of this Agreement, “Trading Day” means a day on which the principal securities exchange on which the Common Shares are then listed or quoted is open for trading. If the vesting condition described in this Section 3.1(c) is not satisfied and the Option has not otherwise become vested pursuant to this Agreement, the Option will expire automatically on the fourth anniversary of the Grant Date. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if (i) the requirements of Section 3.1(b) and (c) were fulfilled as of the fourth anniversary of the Grant Date, and (ii) the Optionee’s employment with the Company and the Partnership ceases due to the Optionee’s death or “Disability”, a termination by the Company or the Partnership other than for “Cause”, or the resignation by the Executive with “Good Reason” (as those terms are defined in that certain Amended and Restated Employment Agreement between the Optionee, the Company and the Partnership entered into on November 20, 2026 (the “Employment Agreement”), on or after the fourth anniversary of the Grant Date and before December 31, 2030, then the Option will vest and become exercisable in full on the date of such cessation of employment. Section 3.2. Change in Control During the Performance Period. Section 5.3(d) of the Plan will not apply to this Option. Instead, and notwithstanding Section 11.3(b) of the Plan, if a Change in Control 3 occurs after the Grant Date and prior to December 31, 2030, the Option will vest and become exercisable in full on either: (a) the date immediately prior to and contingent upon the occurrence of a Change in Control if, as a result of the Change in Control, the Common Shares cease to be publicly traded on a national securities exchange provided that Optionee has been continuously employed by the Company and the Partnership through the Change in Control and provided that the arithmetic mean of the Fair Market Value of a Common Share for the twenty (20) consecutive Trading Days ending with (and including) the date of the Change in Control equals or exceeds the Vesting Trigger Price; or (b) if Section 3.2(a) does not otherwise apply, the fourth (4th) anniversary of the Grant Date provided the following: (i) the Optionee has remained continuously employed by the Company and the Partnership (or a successor thereof in the event of a Change in Control) through and including the date of the Change in Control; (ii) the Common Shares have been continuously listed or quoted for trading on a national securities exchange through the Vesting Target Date; and (iii) the Fair Market Value of a Common Share for the twenty (20) consecutive Trading Days ending with the Vesting Target Date equals or exceeds the Vesting Trigger Price. Provided, however, that for purposes of this Section 3.2(b) only, if the vesting condition described in Section 3.2(b)(ii) cannot be satisfied, the Option will expire automatically at that time. Section 3.3. Death, Disability, Termination other than for Cause, or Resignation for Good Reason During the Performance Period. (a) If prior to December 31, 2030 (or the occurrence of a Change in Control, if sooner) the Optionee’s employment with the Company and the Partnership ceases due to the Optionee’s death or Disability, termination by the Company or the Partnership other than for Cause, or resignation by the Executive with Good Reason, then a pro-rata portion of the Option will vest and become exercisable on the first to occur of (i) the fourth anniversary of the Grant Date if the arithmetic mean of the Fair Market Value of a Common Share for the twenty (20) consecutive Trading Days ending with the Vesting Target Date equals or exceeds the Vesting Trigger Price or (ii) the date a Change in Control occurs provided that the arithmetic mean of the Fair Market Value of a Common Share for the twenty (20) consecutive Trading Days ending with (and including) the date of the Change in Control equals or exceeds the Vesting Trigger Price. (b) Provided that if the vesting condition described in this Section 3.3 is not satisfied and the Option has not otherwise become vested pursuant to this Agreement, the Option will expire automatically on December 31, 2030. (c) The pro-rata portion of the Option described in this Section 3.3 will be equal to a fraction, the numerator of which will be the number of days the Optionee was employed by the Company and the Partnership between the Grant Date and the date his employment ceases, and the denominator of which is 1,461. The remaining portion of the Option will expire automatically upon such cessation of employment. (d) Notwithstanding the foregoing, except in the case of termination due to death, the exercisability of any portion of the Option under this Section 3.3 will be conditioned on (i) the Optionee’s 4 execution and delivery to the Company a release of claims in a form provided by the Company (a “Release”), and (ii) such Release becoming irrevocable within 60 days following such cessation of employment. Section 3.4. Expiration of Option. Notwithstanding any other provision hereof, the Option will expire, and may not be exercised to any extent by anyone, after the first to occur of the following events: (a) December 31, 2036; (b) the second anniversary of the date the Option has become exercisable pursuant to Section 3.3; (c) the cessation of the Optionee’s employment with the Company and the Partnership, if (i) Cause then exists (regardless of the date of such cessation) or (ii) the cessation of the Optionee’s employment occurs before the earlier of December 31, 2030 or a Change in Control, and is either (A) not described in Section 3.3; or (B) described in Section 3.3, but the conditions described in Section 3.3(d) are not satisfied; or (d) the Optionee’s material breach of any restrictive covenant with the Company, the Partnership or any Subsidiary (including, but not limited to, the non-competition, confidentiality, non- solicitation and non-disparagement provisions of the Employment Agreement and any similar restrictive covenant applicable to the Optionee). For avoidance of doubt, the expiration of the Option upon material breach of restrictive covenants will be in addition to, not in lieu of, any other rights or remedies available to the Company, the Partnership or any Subsidiary at law or in equity. ARTICLE IV EXERCISE OF OPTION Section 4.1. Person Eligible to Exercise During the lifetime of the Optionee, only the Optionee may exercise the Option or any portion thereof. After the death of the Optionee, any exercisable portion of the Option may, prior to the time when the Option becomes un-exercisable under Section 3.4, be exercised by the Optionee’s personal representative or by any person empowered to do so under the Optionee’s will or under the then applicable laws of descent and distribution. Section 4.2. Partial Exercise Any exercisable portion of the Option may be exercised in whole or in part at any time prior to the time when the Option or portion thereof becomes un-exercisable under Section 3.4; provided, however, that each partial exercise shall be for not less than Five Hundred (500) Common Shares and shall be for whole Common Shares only. Section 4.3. Manner of Exercise The Option, or any exercisable portion thereof, may be exercised solely by delivery of all of the following to the Secretary (or any third-party administrator or other person or entity designated by the Company for such purpose) prior to the time when the Option or such portion becomes un-exercisable under Section 3.4. 5 (a) Notice in writing signed by the Optionee or any other person then entitled to exercise the Option or portion pursuant to Section 4.1, stating that the Option or portion is thereby exercised, such notice complying with all applicable rules established by the Committee; and (i) Full payment (in cash or check) for the Common Shares with respect to which such Option or portion is exercised; or (ii) With the consent of the Committee, (A) Common Shares owned by the Optionee duly endorsed for transfer to the Company or (B) Common Shares issuable to the Optionee upon exercise of the Option, in each case with a Fair Market Value on the date of Option exercise equal to the aggregate purchase price of the Common Shares with respect to which such Option or portion is exercised; or (iii) A notice that the Optionee has placed a market sell order with a broker with respect to Common Shares then issuable upon exercise of the Option, and that the broker has been directed to pay a sufficient portion of the net proceeds of the sale to the Company in satisfaction of the aggregate exercise price; provided, that payment of such proceeds is then made to the Company upon settlement of such sale; or (iv) With the consent of the Committee, any combination of the consideration provided in Sections 4.3(a)(i), (ii) and (iii); and (b) Such representations and documents as the Committee, in its sole discretion, deems necessary or advisable to effect compliance with all applicable provisions of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the “Securities Act”), and any other federal or state securities laws or regulations. The Committee may, in its sole discretion, also take whatever additional actions it deems appropriate to effect such compliance, including placing legends on share certificates and issuing stop-transfer notices to agents and registrars; and (c) Full payment to the Company (or other employer entity) of all amounts that, under federal, state or local tax law, it is required to withhold upon exercise of the Option. With the consent of the Committee, (i) Common Shares owned by the Optionee duly endorsed for transfer, or (ii) Common Shares issuable to the Optionee upon exercise of the Option may be used to make all or part of such payment; and (d) In the event the Option or portion shall be exercised pursuant to Section 4.1 by any person or persons other than the Optionee, appropriate proof of the right of such person or persons to exercise the Option. Section 4.4. Conditions to Issuance of Common Shares The Common Shares deliverable upon the exercise of the Option, or any portion thereof, may be either previously authorized but unissued Common Shares or issued Common Shares that have then been reacquired by the Company. Such Common Shares shall be fully paid and nonassessable. The Company shall not be required to issue or deliver any certificate or certificates for Common Shares purchased upon the exercise of the Option or portion thereof prior to fulfillment of all of the following conditions: (a) The admission of such Common Shares to listing on all stock exchanges on which such class of Common Shares is then listed; and (b) The completion of any registration or other qualification of such Common Shares under any state or federal law or under rulings or regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission or of 6 any other governmental regulatory body that the Committee shall, in its absolute discretion, deem necessary or advisable; and (c) The obtaining of any approval or other clearance from any state or federal governmental agency that the Committee shall, in its absolute discretion, determine to be necessary or advisable; and (d) The payment to the Company (or other employer entity) of all amounts that, under federal, state or local tax law, it is required to withhold upon exercise of the Option. Section 4.5. Issuance of Common Shares Upon exercise of the Option and satisfaction of the delivery requirements set forth in Section 4.3 and the conditions to the issuance of the Common Shares set forth in Section 4.4, the Company shall issue to the Optionee or the person authorized to exercise the Option under Section 4.1 the Common Shares with respect to which the Option was exercised. Such issuance shall be evidenced by the appropriate entry on the books of the Company or of a duly authorized transfer agent of the Company. ARTICLE V OTHER PROVISIONS Section 5.1. Administration The Committee shall have the power to interpret the Plan and this Agreement and to adopt such rules for the administration, interpretation and application of the Plan as are consistent therewith and to interpret, amend or revoke any such rules. All actions taken and all interpretations and determinations made by the Committee in good faith shall be final and binding upon the Optionee, the Company, the Partnership, the Subsidiaries and all other interested persons. No member of the Committee shall be personally liable for any action, determination or interpretation made in good faith with respect to the Plan, this Agreement or the Option. Section 5.2. Option Not Transferable Neither the Option nor any interest or right therein or part thereof shall be liable for the debts, contracts or engagements of the Optionee or his successors in interest or shall be subject to disposition by transfer, alienation, anticipation, pledge, encumbrance, assignment or any other means, whether such disposition be voluntary or involuntary or by operation of law by judgment, levy, attachment, garnishment or any other legal or equitable proceedings (including bankruptcy), and any attempted disposition thereof shall be null and void and of no effect; provided, however, that this Section 5.2 shall not prevent (a) transfers by will or by the applicable laws of descent and distribution, or (b) transfers permitted by the Administrator in accordance with Section 11.1(c) of the Plan. Section 5.3. Rights as Shareholders The Optionee shall not be, nor have the rights or privileges of, a shareholder of the Company, including voting rights and rights to dividends, in respect of any Common Shares purchasable upon exercise of any part of the Option unless and until such Common Shares have been issued by the Company and held of record by the Optionee (as evidenced by the appropriate entry on the books of the Company or of a duly authorized transfer agent of the Company). No adjustment shall be made for any dividend or other right for which the record date is prior to the date the Common Shares are so issued, except as provided in Section 11.3 of the Plan. 7 Section 5.4. Notices Any notice to be given under the terms of this Agreement to the Company shall be addressed to the Company in care of the Secretary at the Company’s principal address, and any notice to be given to the Optionee shall be addressed to the Optionee at the Optionee’s last address reflected in the Company’s records. By a notice given pursuant to this Section 5.4, either party may hereafter designate a different address for notices to be given to such party. Any notice that is required to be given to the Optionee shall, if the Optionee is then deceased, be given to the person entitled to exercise the Option pursuant to Section 4.1 if such person has previously informed the Company of his status and address by written notice under this Section 5.4. Any such notice will be deemed duly given if delivered personally or via nationally recognized overnight delivery service, on the date and at the time so delivered. Section 5.5. Titles and Construction Titles are provided herein for convenience only and are not to serve as a basis for interpretation or construction of this Agreement. The masculine pronoun shall include the feminine and neuter, and the singular the plural, where the context so indicates. Whenever the words “include”, “includes” or “including” are used in this Agreement, they shall be deemed to be followed by the words “but not limited to”. The term “or” is not exclusive. Section 5.6. Governing Law This Agreement has been negotiated and executed in, and shall be administered, interpreted and enforced under the laws of, the State of North Carolina. Section 5.7. Conformity to Securities Laws The Optionee acknowledges that the Plan and this Agreement are intended to conform to the extent necessary with all provisions of the Securities Act and the Exchange Act and any and all regulations and rules promulgated by the Securities and Exchange Commission thereunder, including Rule 16b-3, and state securities laws and regulations. Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, the Plan shall be administered, and the Option is granted and may be exercised, only in such a manner as to conform to such laws, rules and regulations. To the extent permitted by applicable law, the Plan and this Agreement shall be deemed amended to the extent necessary to conform to such laws, rules and regulations. Section 5.8. Consents The Optionee’s rights in respect of the Option are conditioned on the receipt to the full satisfaction of the Committee of any required consents that the Committee may determine to be necessary or advisable (including the Optionee’s consenting to the Company’s supplying to any third-party recordkeeper of the Plan such personal information as the Committee deems advisable to administer the Plan). Section 5.9. Amendments, Suspension and Termination To the extent permitted by the Plan, this Agreement may be wholly or partially amended or otherwise modified, suspended or terminated at any time or from time to time by the Committee; provided that, except as may otherwise be provided by the Plan, no amendment, modification, suspension or termination of this Agreement shall adversely affect the Option in any material way without the prior written consent of the Optionee. 8 Section 5.10. Successors and Assigns The Company may assign any of its rights under this Agreement to single or multiple assignees, and this Agreement shall inure to the benefit of the successors and assigns of the Company. Subject to the restrictions on transfer set forth in Section 5.2, this Agreement shall be binding upon the Optionee and his heirs, executors, administrators, successors and assigns. Section 5.11. Section 409A The Option is not intended to constitute “nonqualified deferred compensation” within the meaning of Section 409A and the Plan and this Agreement shall be interpreted accordingly. Nonetheless, neither the Company nor the Partnership make any guaranty regarding the tax treatment of this Award. Section 5.12. Limitation on Optionee’s Rights Participation in the Plan confers no rights or interests other than as herein provided. This Agreement creates only a contractual obligation on the part of the Company as to amounts payable and shall not be construed as creating a trust. Neither the Plan nor any underlying program, in and of itself, has any assets. The Optionee shall have only the rights of a general unsecured creditor of the Company with respect to amounts credited and benefits payable, if any, with respect to the Option, and rights no greater than those of a general unsecured creditor to receive the Common Shares with respect to the Option, as and when exercised pursuant to the terms hereof. Section 5.13. Clawback. In consideration for the grant of this Award, the Grantee agrees to be subject to (a) any compensation clawback, recoupment or similar policies of the Company, the Partnership or any Subsidiary that may be in effect from time to time, whether adopted before or after the date of this Award (including, without limitation, any clawback policy adopted to comply with the requirements of the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act and any rules or regulations promulgated thereunder), and (b) such other compensation clawbacks as may be required by applicable law ((a) and (b) together, the “Clawback Provisions”). The Grantee acknowledges that the Clawback Provisions are not limited in their application to this Award, or to amounts received in connection with this Award. Section 5.14. Entire Agreement. This Agreement is intended to memorialize the “Renewal Stock Option Award” described in Section 5(d) of the Employment Agreement. The Plan and this Agreement constitute the entire agreement of the parties and supersede in their entirety all prior undertakings and agreements of the Company and the Optionee with respect to that Renewal Stock Option Award (including, without limitation, Section 5(d) of the Employment Agreement). Section 5.15. Counterparts. This Agreement may be signed in counterparts, each of which shall be an original, with the same effect as if the signatures thereto and hereto were upon the same instrument. Section 5.16. Electronic Signature. The parties hereto agree that this Agreement may be delivered and executed by electronic means, and that such electronic delivery and signature will have the same effect as physical delivery and signature. 9 IN WITNESS WHEREOF, this Agreement has been executed and delivered by the parties hereto. TANGER INC. By: Michael J. Bilerman Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Investment Officer TANGER PROPERTIES LIMITED PARTNERSHIP By: TANGER, Inc., its sole general partner By: /s/ Michael J. Bilerman Michael J. Bilerman Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Chief Investment Officer Optionee: Stephen Yalof Optionee’s Taxpayer ID Number Date /s/ Michael J. text: EX-10.1 2 exhibit101-expensereimburs.htm EX-10.1 Document EXHIBIT 10.1 EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT AGREEMENT This EXPENSE REIMBURSEMENT AGREEMENT (this “Agreement” ) is entered into effective November 15, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”) by VAST HOLDINGS, INC. , an Oklahoma corporation ( “Holdings” ), VAST BANK, NATIONAL ASSOCIATION , a national banking association (the “Bank” ), and USBC, INC. , a Nevada corporation (the “Reimbursing Party”). Each signatory is a “ Party ,” and together they are the “ Parties .” The Reimbursing Party agrees to provide expense reimbursements directly to Holdings for eligible Bank expenses, subject to the applicable Reimbursement Cap and credits for reimbursements received, and Holdings agrees to transfer those reimbursements to the Bank, on the terms below. Section 1. Expense Reimbursements; Defined Terms . The Reimbursing Party hereby agrees to reimburse the full Reimbursement Amount in accordance with an Approved Expense Budget and this Agreement. The Reimbursing Party shall not receive services, commercial consideration, ownership or operating rights, or any other monetary or non-monetary compensation in exchange. The obligation of the Reimbursing Party shall remain effective during the Term of this Agreement, as defined below, and survives as provided in Section 8. “ Approved Expense Budget ” means the budget approved by the Parties with respect to a given expense period that identifies the expense period, the eligible expense categories, monthly projections, and the Reimbursement Cap (as defined below). Each Approved Expense Budget shall contain sufficient detail as deemed reasonable and necessary by the Parties, including, but not limited to, projected expenses and reimbursements by product or service, cost categories, and Bank positions by title. With respect to personnel expense, the Approved Expense Budget shall state the cost allocated to Eligible Expenses and reduce such projected reimbursement by cost allocated to core banking operations. “ Business Day ” means a day other than Saturday, Sunday, or a day on which Federal Reserve Banks are closed for a federal holiday. “Expense Month ” means a calendar month, or covered portion of a month, to which Eligible Expenses are attributable under an Approved Expense Budget. “ Reimbursement Amount ” means the full Eligible Expenses for an Expense Month taking into account amounts invoiced, where applicable, and actually received by the Bank in such Expense Month from products and services to which Eligible Expenses are attributed. The Reimbursement Amount shall not be less than zero and is subject to the Reimbursement Cap. Under no circumstances shall determination of a Reimbursement Amount create any amount payable by Holdings or the Bank to the Reimbursing Party or any credit or carryforward to another Expense Month. Actual overpayments remain subject to Section 4(e). “ Reimbursement Cap ” means a fixed cap on aggregate reimbursements under this Agreement for a given expense period. The Reimbursement Cap is a maximum reimbursement commitment and does not require payment of unused budget. 1 Section 2. Approved Expense Budgets . The Parties shall separately approve an interim budget for the expense period beginning October 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 (the “ Interim Budget ”), and an annual budget for January 1 through December 31, 2027 (the “ Annual Budget ”). The approved Interim Budget is attached hereto as Schedule 1. The Bank and Holdings shall deliver the proposed Annual Budget to the Reimbursing Party by December 11, 2026, and all Parties must approve it in writing before January 1, 2027. Each of the Interim Budget and the Annual Budget shall be an Approved Expense Budget. The Interim Budget is subject to a separate Reimbursement Cap for the period through December 31, 2026. The Reimbursing Party is responsible for the full eligible unpaid amount within the Reimbursement Cap. Actual expenses and changes in projections or methodology do not increase the Reimbursement Cap. Changes to this Agreement’s categories, covered expense period, methodology or Reimbursement Cap require written approval by all Parties under Section 9. Except for credits under Section 4(e), release of an accrued claim requires an express written release by the Bank and Holdings. Unused Interim Budget capacity does not increase the Reimbursement Cap for the Annual Budget. Signing this Agreement does not approve an incomplete budget. No expense attributable to a period before October 1, 2026 is eligible under this Agreement. Section 3. Eligible Expenses and Permitted Uses . “ Eligible Expenses ” are actual, documented costs of the Bank’s own business that are attributable to an expense period covered by an Approved Expense Budget, comply with the Bank’s expense policies, have been paid by the Bank, and otherwise satisfy the Approved Expense Budget. They are limited to approved salaries, operational and technology expenses, legal and consulting fees, travel, and other expressly approved costs. Salary eligibility, period attribution, and other recoveries are subject to agreement by the Parties as part of an Approved Expense Budget. A preexisting employment or vendor arrangement may generate Eligible Expenses for a covered prospective period, including the Interim Budget period. The inclusion of an expenditure does not determine its accounting or tax classification. (a) Allocation and duplication . Each cost shall be assigned to its product or service and expense period at actual cost without a markup or program-management fee. Charges under a separate administrative services agreement with the Bank remain governed by that agreement. The underlying cost may not also be recovered as a Bank Eligible Expense to the extent recovered through that charge or another reimbursement. Payroll support, third-party credits, refunds, and other recoveries shall be reflected consistently to prevent duplicate recovery. (b) Excluded uses . Eligible Expenses exclude expenses or liabilities of the Reimbursing Party or any affiliate other than the Bank, distributions to owners, settlement of historical intercompany balances prior to the Interim Budget period, affiliate loans, and costs of services or deliverables for the Reimbursing Party. An expense outside the Approved Expense Budget or in excess of an express limit does not create an automatic reimbursement obligation. Section 4. Reimbursement Obligations and Timing . 2 (a) Direct reimbursement obligation . The Reimbursing Party shall pay the full Reimbursement Amount, subject to the applicable Reimbursement Cap and Section 4(f). (b) Monthly statement . Within ten (10) Business Days after each Expense Month ends, Holdings and the Bank shall prepare, and Holdings shall deliver to the Reimbursing Party, a monthly statement with reasonable supporting records. The statement shall identify the budget; actual paid Eligible Expenses by business line and period; actual adjustments; the Reimbursement Amount; amounts claimed, received, and transferred to the Bank; material variances; and remaining budget capacity. The Bank shall provide its information to Holdings in time for delivery. Protected records may be furnished as permitted by Section 7. For purposes of this subsection, the required monthly statement and supporting materials for October 2026 have already been submitted to the Reimbursing Party and the payment deadline in Section 4(c) remains applicable. (c) Payment timing; review . Each monthly Reimbursement Amount is due in immediately available U.S. funds to Holdings’ designated account no later than three (3) Business Days before the end of the succeeding month (the “ Payment Date ”). The Reimbursing Party shall review each request for reimbursement promptly and approve it or identify any specific, good-faith objection, with the amount and reason, before the Payment Date. (d) Reconciliation. Within thirty (30) calendar days after each calendar quarter ends, Holdings shall provide the Reimbursing Party a reconciliation showing claims under this Agreement, actual payments, credits, adjustments, Bank transfers, and remaining capacity for the Approved Expense Budget. The same cost, payment, or claim shall not be counted twice. (e) Overpayments. Only an actual duplicate payment, calculation error, ineligible reimbursement, or later credit or recovery attributable to the original claim and Expense Month creates an overpayment. Receipts attributable to a later Expense Month, later profitability, or an increase in the value of the Bank or its business do not create an overpayment or a right to recover a reimbursement properly paid for an earlier Expense Month. Holdings shall return a substantiated overpayment to the Reimbursing Party, or apply an agreed credit, within five (5) Business Days after the amount is agreed or otherwise determined. The Bank shall return to Holdings only the portion it actually received and only to the extent independently permissible. (f) Payments and satisfaction of obligations . Each reimbursement received by Holdings from the Reimbursing Party and applied to identified Eligible Expenses shall automatically satisfy the corresponding reimbursement obligation under this Agreement to the extent paid. No Eligible Expense may be recovered more than once and actual duplicates and other overpayments are governed by Section 4(e). The Reimbursing Party’s payment creates no repayment, contribution, indemnity, or subrogation right against the Bank or Holdings, except an actual overpayment under Section 4(e). Section 5. Bank Protection . (a) Payment to the Bank . Holdings shall transfer to the Bank, in immediately available cash, the Reimbursement Amount promptly after actual receipt. Holdings shall not 3 defer remittance for additional internal approvals or cash-management purposes. These requirements apply to regular, supplemental, and resolved disputed reimbursements. The timing of each transfer and the treatment of any resulting receivable remain subject to Section 6. (b) Obligations . Holdings shall not retain or divert the Bank’s reimbursement to its own expenses or another affiliate, except to replenish an amount Holdings has already paid to the Bank for the same Eligible Expenses. Each Bank claim is payable only once. The Bank may enforce Holdings’ payment obligation directly. A deposit standing in Holdings’ name at the Bank is not payment to the Bank; payment requires an actual transfer for the Bank’s own account. The Bank shall not purchase, discount, acquire by assignment, or give consideration for Holdings’ reimbursement claim against the Reimbursing Party. The Bank’s rights under this Agreement do not depend on acquiring that claim. (c) Bank expenses and liquidity . Monthly reimbursement in arrears applies to the Bank’s own expenses incurred for its independently conducted business. The Bank remains responsible for its own wages, contracts, regulatory duties, and other liabilities. It is not required to incur all budgeted expenses or make a new commitment in reliance on an unpaid reimbursement. The Bank’s rights to decline commitments, suspend performance, and terminate are governed by Sections 6 and 8, without impairing lawful accrued reimbursement obligations. (d) Affiliate liabilities and shortfalls . Holdings shall pay its own liabilities directly. If the Bank would incur or pay a liability on behalf of Holdings or another affiliate, the responsible affiliate must first provide the Bank with sufficient available cash, unless a separate transaction has been approved and documented in compliance with Section 6 before any credit arises. Monthly arrears under this Agreement do not apply to such affiliate liabilities. The Bank and Holdings shall monitor payment timing, receivables, and liquidity; notify the Reimbursing Party promptly of a missed payment or material shortfall; and take the action required by Section 6. A budget overrun requires a written budget amendment and does not authorize an affiliate advance. Section 6. Regulation W and Bank Independence . (a) No authorized affiliate credit . This Agreement does not authorize the Bank to lend to an affiliate, acquire an affiliate obligation in a transaction constituting affiliate credit, guarantee an affiliate’s liabilities, pledge Bank assets, or enter into a cross-affiliate netting arrangement. No payment period or reconciliation deadline is a grace period under sections 23A or 23B of the Federal Reserve Act or Regulation W. A transaction that constitutes affiliate credit must be separately approved and documented before it occurs and satisfy all applicable quantitative limits, collateral, market terms, safety-and-soundness, and reporting requirements, or a properly documented applicable exemption. A reimbursement promise or affiliate guarantee is not a substitute for required cash or eligible collateral. (b) Terms and monitoring . The Bank shall monitor affiliate receivables and payment practices and document the basis for their regulatory treatment. Where section 23B applies, terms must be substantially the same as, or at least as favorable to the Bank as, comparable nonaffiliate terms, or the applicable good-faith standard where comparables do not 4 exist. If a transaction or delay would be impermissible, the Reimbursing Party shall provide earlier payment or change the mechanics before the exposure arises; if a violation nevertheless occurs, it shall promptly correct it and make any required report. The Bank may require suspension of new affected commitments or other lawful protective action under Section 8 without waiting for an amendment. A return of money by the Bank must be a substantiated overpayment under Section 4(e) and independently permissible. (c) No services or commercial rights . Neither Holdings nor the Bank is required by this Agreement to perform, procure, subcontract, or cause services or deliverables for the Reimbursing Party. The Reimbursing Party shall not acquire equity, a conversion right, a preferential return, a license, intellectual-property rights, customer access, or operating or governance authority. The Bank independently determines its lawful activities, staffing, vendors, products, and technology. Budget consent determines the amount and eligible use of support; it does not authorize direction of Bank operations. The Bank retains its rights in work developed for its own business, subject to independently existing third-party rights. No Reimbursement Amount constitutes a payment, distribution, assignment, or transfer of Bank assets or income to the Reimbursing Party. The Reimbursing Party acquires, under or by reason of this Agreement, no ownership interest in, entitlement to, or right to share in the Bank’s or Holdings’ receipts, income, earnings, profits, cash flow, appreciation, or proceeds of any sale or other disposition. No reimbursement entitles the Reimbursing Party to a distribution, royalty, return on reimbursement, or recoupment from future business performance. These limitations apply during and after the Term, regardless of the amount of reimbursements provided, the financial performance of any business line, or whether the Bank or Holdings becomes profitable. Neither an Approved Expense Budget nor any report, reconciliation, review, approval, or reimbursement creates or implies any such right. Section 7. Records, Confidentiality, and Regulatory Access . Each Party shall maintain records sufficient to substantiate its obligations and payments. The Reimbursing Party may review reasonably necessary cost and application records through Holdings to verify funding use. Such review is financial substantiation only and creates no consulting, development, or other services undertaking. The Parties shall protect nonpublic information, limit access to persons with a need to know and appropriate confidentiality duties, and comply with customer-information, privilege, and confidential-supervisory-information restrictions. Records shall be retained as required by law and applicable retention policies. Each Party shall permit lawful examination by regulators with jurisdiction and provide required information without conditioning lawful regulatory access on another Party’s consent. These obligations survive termination. Section 8. Term, Termination, and Final Reconciliation. This Agreement continues through December 31, 2027 (the “ Term ”) unless terminated earlier under this Section. No new budget is required after termination, and no unapproved future period is funded by implication. Nothing requires Holdings or the Bank to undertake new activity merely to exhaust a budget. The Reimbursing Party may terminate this Agreement upon sixty (60) days’ written notice to Holdings and the Bank. Upon delivering such notice, this Agreement shall terminate on 5 the last calendar day of the month in which the notice period ends. The Bank or Holdings may, in its sole discretion, immediately suspend an affected activity or terminate this Agreement if it determines that doing so is necessary or advisable to comply with applicable law, regulation, or regulatory guidance. Suspension or termination does not discharge lawful reimbursement obligations for otherwise Eligible Expenses attributable to covered expense periods before the effective date of such suspension or termination, subject to the other limitations in this Agreement. Accrued lawful payment obligations, limited excess-fund returns, and record obligations survive. The provisions governing determination of the Reimbursement Amount, the limitations on overpayment claims in Section 4(e), and the disclaimers in Section 6(c) survive expiration or termination of this Agreement and completion of any reconciliation. Within thirty (30) calendar days after the last applicable expense period, approved wind-down commitment ends, or, if earlier, after the effective date of any termination, Holdings shall deliver the final reconciliation; undisputed amounts shall be settled under Section 5. No termination, funding lapse, or dispute revives a discontinued services obligation under another agreement. Section 9. General Provisions . This Agreement and each Approved Expense Budget constitute the entire agreement concerning the obligation of the Reimbursing Party to reimburse expenses. No Approved Expense Budget overrides Sections 5 through 8 or creates services, credit, equity, or other commercial rights. All amendments require a writing signed by all Parties and their required approvals. Each Party represents that it has authority to enter into and perform this Agreement. No Party may assign an obligation or substitute a payer without the Parties’ written consent. Each Party bears its own costs of negotiating this Agreement unless separately agreed in a manner consistent with applicable law. This Agreement is governed by applicable federal law and the laws of Oklahoma. Notices and budget approvals shall be delivered to the authorized representatives and addresses designated in Schedule 1 or by subsequent written notice and are effective on actual receipt. Electronic delivery is permitted. A failure to enforce a provision is not a waiver. An unenforceable provision shall be severed only to the extent necessary without enlarging the Bank’s obligations or reviving discontinued services. There are no third-party beneficiaries. Counterparts and electronic signatures are effective to the extent permitted by law. 6 SIGNATURES Each Party has caused this Agreement to be executed and delivered by its duly authorized representative as of the Effective Date. Execution also approves the completed initial Schedule 1 attached to this Agreement. VAST HOLDINGS, INC. By: /s/ Linda Jenkinson Name: Linda Jenkinson Title: Chair & CEO VAST BANK, N.A. By: /s/ Mike Kozub Name: Mike Kozub Title: CEO USBC, INC. text: EX-10.2 3 exhibit102-terminationandp.htm EX-10.2 Document EXHIBIT 10.2 TERMINATION AND PRESERVATION OF EXISTING CLAIMS AGREEMENT This TERMINATION AND PRESERVATION OF EXISTING CLAIMS AGREEMENT (this “Agreement” ) is entered into as of November 15, 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”) by VAST HOLDINGS, INC. , an Oklahoma corporation ( “Holdings” ), and USBC, INC. , a Nevada corporation ( “USBC” ), each a “Party” and together the “ Parties .” The Parties agree to end their services arrangement for future performance and preserve existing historical rights and defenses on the terms stated below. Section 1. Prior Agreements . The “ Prior Agreements ” are (i) the Affiliate Services Agreement dated March 18, 2026 between Holdings and USBC (the “ Services Agreement ”) and (ii) their Acknowledgment and Agreement dated March 31, 2026 (the “ Acknowledgment ”). The defined term “Bank” in those instruments identifies Holdings. Vast Bank, N.A. (the “ Bank ”) is not a party to either Prior Agreement or to this Agreement. Section 2. Termination of the Services Arrangement . As of the Effective Date, the Prior Agreements terminate for future performance, subject only to the historical matters expressly preserved in Sections 3 and 4; provided, however, that this Agreement shall not be effective unless and until the Expense Reimbursement Agreement by and among Holdings, USBC, and Vast Bank, N.A. has been fully executed. Holdings has no further obligation under either Prior Agreement to perform, provide, arrange, procure, subcontract, or otherwise cause services, deliverables, or business activities to be performed for or on behalf of USBC. USBC has no further right under either Prior Agreement to require that performance. These provisions apply to all services under the Prior Agreements, including Tokenized Deposit Services and Fair Access Services, regardless of the label used. Except for Existing Claims as defined in Section 3, below, no fee, expense reimbursement, payment, or guaranty obligation accrues under the Prior Agreements for services performed or costs incurred after the Effective Date. No unused budget or reimbursement cap authorizes new work or expenditures. Any renewal, survival, incorporation, precedence, or other provision of a Prior Agreement is subject to this express termination and cannot continue or revive a future service obligation. This Agreement effects an immediate mutual termination at the Effective Date. Neither Party must wait for a notice period to expire, and the Parties dispense with any notice or cure period solely to accomplish this mutual termination. The termination does not transfer any obligation to the Bank or authorize services by that bank for USBC. Section 3. Existing Claims and Historical Matters . (a) Scope of preservation . “ Existing Claims ” means monetary rights, obligations, claims, and related defenses under the Prior Agreements attributable to services performed, costs incurred, or other events occurring before the Effective Date. A later invoice or payment date does not make an otherwise historical matter prospective. No Existing Claim requires future service performance for USBC. 1 (b) Original conditions and limitations . Each Existing Claim is preserved only to the extent it exists under the applicable Prior Agreement and law, subject to its original eligibility, prior approval, allocation, documentation, calculation, payment, cap, limitation, credit, and defense provisions. Qualifying Pre-Term Services under the Acknowledgment remain subject to its original restrictions, including the applicable vendor and service-period conditions, and count within the same $10,500,000 cap under the Services Agreement. (c) No admission or change of debt . Neither Party admits the validity, amount, enforceability, payment status, or triggering event of an Existing Claim. This Agreement does not release, accelerate, recharacterize, or change the obligor of an Existing Claim. (d) Payment and resolution . Existing payment deadlines and any payment-during-dispute requirements applicable to valid obligations remain unchanged. Reconciliation and discussions do not defer an amount otherwise properly due. Neither reconciliation nor execution of a separate agreement is a condition to the termination in Section 2. Section 4. Historical Records and Continuing Protections . The definitions, fee calculations, invoice-review and audit rights, recordkeeping, confidentiality, regulatory-access, dispute, governing-law, and other provisions of the Prior Agreements necessary to determine and resolve Existing Claims remain applicable. The Parties shall cooperate in exchanging reasonably available records needed to identify and resolve Existing Claims, subject to applicable confidentiality, privilege, customer-information, and supervisory-information restrictions. No surviving provision authorizes future performance of the discontinued services. Section 5. Separate Arrangements and Future Support . This Agreement addresses only the Prior Agreements. It does not amend or discharge any separate Bank– Holdings agreement, the January 1, 2026 agreement between USBC and Vast Bank, N.A., any agreement with Hard Yaka Ventures Management Co., LLC or another Hard Yaka entity, or any separate commercial arrangement. It does not determine the validity, enforceability, payment status, or regulatory treatment of any such arrangement. This Agreement creates no new funding commitment or right to invoice USBC for future Bank or Holdings operating or development costs. Any future support requires a separate agreement naming the actual funder and recipient and obtaining the required approvals. This Agreement grants no new rights and determines no accounting, tax, or regulatory-capital classification. Section 6. General Provisions . This Agreement is the entire agreement of the Parties concerning the prospective termination of the Prior Agreements, subject to Sections 3 and 4, and controls over any inconsistent provision of either Prior Agreement. It does not generally ratify the Prior Agreements or past conduct. Further amendment requires a writing signed by both Parties. No person other than a Party obtains a new right or obligation under this Agreement. 2 This Agreement is governed by applicable federal law and the laws of Oklahoma, without regard to conflict-of-laws rules. If a provision is unenforceable, the remaining provisions continue to the extent permitted by law; no such determination automatically revives a terminated service obligation. A waiver of one breach is not a waiver of another. Notices and counterpart deliveries shall be in writing and are effective when received, including by electronic delivery to an address designated by the receiving Party. This Agreement binds the Parties and their permitted successors and assigns. It may be executed in counterparts that together constitute one instrument. Electronic signatures and delivery are effective to the extent permitted by law. Each signatory represents that the signatory is authorized to execute and deliver this Agreement for the identified Party. 3 SIGNATURES Each Party has caused this Agreement to be executed and delivered by its duly authorized representative as of the Effective Date. VAST HOLDINGS, INC. By: /s/ Linda Jenkinson Name: Linda Jenkinson Title: Chair & CEO USBC, INC. By: /s/ Dan Beck Name: Dan Beck Title: Chief Financial Officer 4

text: EX-10.1 2 d167441dex101.htm EX-10.1 EX-10.1 Exhibit 10.1 Insulet Corporation 100 Nagog Park, Acton, MA 01720 November 17, 2026 Todd Trapp [Address on file] Dear Todd: Insulet Corporation (“Insulet” or the “Company”) is pleased to offer you the full-time position of Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer , reporting directly to Ashley McEvoy, President and Chief Executive Officer . Your principal place of employment will be at the Company’s headquarters in Acton, Massachusetts. We are excited about the prospect of you joining Insulet and look forward to your meaningful contribution to the team. Your first day of employment will be December 7, 2026 . Your annual base salary will be $750,000 , paid on a bi-weekly basis, in accordance with the Company’s normal payroll practices as established or modified from time to time. You are eligible to participate in our annual bonus program beginning calendar year 2027, with a target of 80% of your base salary . Payout typically takes place in the first quarter following the end of the calendar plan year. The design of the Company’s annual bonus program will be determined by the Company and there are no guarantees with respect to how any design changes will affect future bonus payments to you. The Company is committed to sharing its continued success with its employees through long-term incentive opportunities. You will be eligible to participate in the Company’s long-term incentive (LTI) program, with an annual LTI target of $4,000,000 . The design of the Company’s annual equity program will be determined by the Company and there are no guarantees with respect to how any design changes will affect future equity awards to you. Awards are discretionary and not guaranteed. Your 2027 annual LTI award will be granted to you in February 2027 with 50% of this award provided to you in the form of performance restricted stock units (PSUs), 25% in the form of restricted stock units (“RSUs”) and 25% in the form of non-qualified stock options (“NSOs”). The award value will be converted to PSUs, RSUs and NSOs (each subject to rounding down to the nearest whole share) based on the closing price of a share of Insulet common stock on the grant date. PSUs vest subject to the performance criteria and vesting provisions over a three-year performance period. RSUs will vest in substantially equal installments on the first, second, and third anniversaries of the grant date. NSOs will vest in substantially equal installments on the first, second, third, and fourth anniversaries of the grant date. NASDAQ PODD | Insulet.com You will receive a sign-on equity award, with a grant date fair value of $3,500,000 , which will be delivered to you in the form of RSUs. The actual number of RSUs granted to you for your sign-on award will be calculated by dividing the dollar value of the RSU award by the closing price of a share of Insulet common stock on the grant date. These RSUs will vest in substantially equal installments on the first, second, and third anniversary of the grant date. Your sign-on equity award will be granted on the first trading day of the month following the month in which you commence employment, based on our monthly grant cadence. Assuming a December 7, 2026 start date, this would mean a grant date of January 1, 2027. The material terms of your sign-on award as well as your annual grant will be contained in the applicable award agreements be issued to you at the time of grant. The terms and conditions document under which each award is issued shall govern. The Company will pay you a signing bonus totaling $1,000,000 , divided into two components: (i) $500,000 payable immediately following your hire date in December 2026 (the “Initial Sign-On Bonus”), and (ii) $500,000 payable in June 2027, provided you remain continuously employed by the Company through that date (the “Secondary Sign-On Bonus”). Both payments will be treated as taxable income. If you voluntarily terminate your employment with the Company or are terminated for “Cause” (as defined by the Company), within twelve (12) months following the payment of either bonus, you will be required to repay the full amount of the applicable bonus. Each bonus is subject to its own twelve (12) month clawback period, beginning on the date the respective bonus is paid. From your first day of employment through March 31 st , 2027, Insulet will cover your travel expenses for regular visits to Acton and other Company sites as requested by the CEO or required needs of the business, in accordance with the Insulet Travel and Expense Policy. For accommodations beyond March 31, 2027, you will receive a lump -sum payment of $200,000 to support your establishment of long -term housing or accommodations in or near Acton. You will be expected to maintain a regular presence in Acton and/or other company sites. If you voluntarily terminate your employment with Insulet (or are terminated for Cause) within 24 months of your start date, you must repay part of the lump-sum payment, prorated for the number of days left in that 24-month period. You are eligible for severance and change in control benefits pursuant and subject to the terms of the Insulet Corporation Amended and Restated Executive Severance Plan. You will also be eligible to participate in the Company’s benefits programs to the same extent as, and subject to the same terms, conditions, and limitations applicable to, other similarly situated employees of the Company. For a more detailed understanding of the benefits and the applicable eligibility requirements, please consult the applicable summary plan descriptions. In order to protect Insulet’s substantial investment of time and money in the creation and maintaining of its confidential information and good-will with its customers and business partners, all employees are required to execute the Company’s standard confidential information and restrictive covenant agreement as a condition of employment with Insulet. Further, Insulet 978.600.7000 NASDAQ PODD Insulet.com respects any obligations you may have with your current/former employer(s) (including safeguarding its confidential information), and we expect you to honor them as well. To that end, you confirm that you will not remove or copy any documents or proprietary data or materials of any kind, electronic or otherwise, from your current or former employer to Insulet without written authorization from your current/former employer, nor will you use or disclose any such confidential information during the course and scope of your employment with Insulet. While we are hopeful and confident that our relationship will be mutually rewarding, satisfactory and sustaining, this letter shall not be construed as an agreement, either express or implied, to employ you for any stated term and shall in no way alter Insulet’s policy of employment at will, under which both you and Insulet remain free to end the employment relationship, for any reason, at any time, with or without notice. Similarly, nothing in this letter shall be construed as an agreement, either express or implied, to pay you any compensation or grant you any benefit beyond the end of your employment with Insulet. Please note, this offer of employment is contingent on: (i) verification of your right to work in the United States, as demonstrated by your completion of the Form I-9 upon hire and your submission of acceptable documentation (as noted on the Form I-9) verifying your identity and work authorization within three (3) days of starting employment; (ii) satisfactory completion of a background investigation, for which the required notice and consent forms shall be emailed to you after execution of this Offer Letter; (iii) execution of Insulet’s Confidential Information and Restrictive Covenant Agreement prior to your start date; and (iv) Insulet receiving verification that you hold the qualification(s) for the Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer position. This offer will be withdrawn if any of the above conditions are not satisfied. This letter constitutes our entire offer regarding the terms and conditions of your employment by Insulet, and it supersedes any prior agreements or other promises or statements (whether oral or written) regarding the offered terms of employment. Other than with respect to specific terms set forth herein, as an executive officer, your compensation will be determined annually by Talent and Compensation Committee of the Board of Directors in its sole discretion. It is with great pleasure that we welcome you to Insulet! We recognize that our success is the direct result of the contributions made by our dedicated and talented workforce. We look forward to further strengthening the Insulet team with your contributions. Best regards, /s/ Lisa Blair Davis Lisa Blair Davis Senior Vice President, Chief Human Resources Officer 978.600.7000 NASDAQ PODD Insulet.com Acceptance: Your signature below confirms your acceptance of the offer to join Insulet as Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and also confirms you have reviewed the job description for this position and that you meet the minimum qualifications required of this role. Todd Trapp Signature /s/ Todd Trapp 11/18/2026 978.600.7000 NASDAQ PODD Insulet.com
