title: ODYSSEY MARINE EXPLORATION INC
text: EX-10.7 8 d191731dex107.htm EX-10.7 EX-10.7 Exhibit 10.7 [FORM OF] ASSIGNMENT AND ASSUMPTION AGREEMENT This Assignment and Assumption Agreement (this “ Agreement ”), dated [ DATE ], 2026 (the “ Effective Date ”), is entered into by and among Odyssey Marine Exploration, Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “ Assignor ”), Pacific Critical Minerals, Inc., a Nevada corporation (the “ Assignee ”), and Poplar Falls LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the “ Funder ”) (each individually, a “ Party ,” and collectively, the “ Parties ”). Capitalized terms used but not defined herein shall have the definitions ascribed to them in the ORM Services Agreement or the ICEA (each as defined below). W I T N E S S E T H: WHEREAS , concurrently with the execution of this Agreement, the Assignor and Assignee will execute a services agreement, pursuant to which Assignor will provide various services to Assignee (the “ ORM Services Agreement ”); WHEREAS , Oceánica Resources México, S. de R.L. de C.V., a company incorporated in Mexico and an indirect subsidiary of the Assignor (“ ORM ”) holds, directly or indirectly, (i) 50% of the outstanding equity interests in Phosagmex, S.A.P.I. de C.V., a company organized in Mexico (“ Phosagmex ”), and (ii) 99.99% of the outstanding equity interests in Exploraciones Oceánicas, S. de R.L. de C.V., a company incorporated in Mexico (“ ExO ”); WHEREAS , the Assignor, ExO, and the Funder are parties to the Third Amended and Restated International Claims Enforcement Agreement, dated as of June 14, 2021 (the “ ICEA ”), pursuant to which the Funder has provided funding in connection with the Subject Claims and the Arbitral Award; WHEREAS , the Assignor, Oceanus Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation (“ Merger Sub ”) and wholly owned subsidiary of the Assignor, and American Ocean Minerals Corporation (“ AOM ”) entered into that certain Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of April 8, 2026 (as amended, the “ Merger Agreement ”), pursuant to which Merger Sub will merge with and into AOM, with AOM continuing as the surviving corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of the Assignor (the “ Merger ”); WHEREAS , in accordance with the Merger Agreement, the Pre-Closing Reorganization (as such term is defined in the Merger Agreement) and the other transactions contemplated therein have been completed or will be completed on or prior to the Closing Date (as such term is defined in the Merger Agreement); WHEREAS , as part of the Pre-Closing Reorganization, Assignee was formed on [DATE], 2026, to hold and preserve the value of ORM and its subsidiaries (including its equity interests in Phosagmex and ExO) (the “ ORM Entities ”) and any assets owned by the ORM Entities (collectively, the “ ORM Assets ”); WHEREAS , the Merger Agreement contemplates and requires the execution and delivery of this Agreement by the Parties immediately prior to the Closing (as defined in the Merger Agreement) of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement; and 1 WHEREAS , the Parties desire to enter into this Agreement for the purpose of having the Assignor assign to the Assignee its obligations under the ICEA as part of the Pre-Closing Reorganization and as required under the Merger Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE , in consideration of the mutual agreements and covenants set forth herein, the Parties hereby agree as follows: 1. Assignment and Assumption; Assignor Continuing Obligations (a) Subject to the satisfaction (or waiver) of the conditions set forth in Section 4 , effective as of the Closing Date, the Assignor hereby irrevocably assigns, transfers, conveys, and delivers to the Assignee all of the Assignor’s obligations, rights and interest in or under the ICEA; provided , however , that notwithstanding such assignment, Assignor will continue to be bound by the ICEA Continuing Obligations (as defined below). (b) Subject to the satisfaction (or waiver) of the conditions set forth in Section 4 , effective as of the Closing Date, the Assignee hereby assumes and will perform and discharge all the obligations, covenants, agreements, undertakings, and liabilities of the Assignor under the ICEA, howsoever arising, whether direct or indirect, absolute or contingent, present or future, matured or not, extended or renewed, wheresoever incurred, and whether the Assignor is bound alone or with others, as a Claimholder. (c) Notwithstanding the assignment and assumption pursuant to the foregoing subsections (a) and (b), Assignor will: (i) provide the Arbitral Award Support Services (as defined in the ORM Services Agreement) as set forth in the ORM Services Agreement; and (ii) retain the following continuing obligations (collectively, the “ ICEA Continuing Obligations ”) under the ICEA as if it were the Claimholder thereunder, with the Assignor to be reimbursed for costs and expenses in accordance with the ORM Services Agreement: (A) Receipt of Proceeds; Claims Escrow Account . Unless otherwise directed by the Funder, the Assignor shall comply with Section 7.1(a) and Section 7.1(b) of the ICEA with respect to any Proceeds received by the Assignor, including by providing the notices and depositing all such Proceeds into the Escrow Account within the time periods required by Section 7.1(a) of the ICEA; (B) Instruction of Nominated Lawyers . The Assignor shall irrevocably instruct the Nominated Lawyers to keep the Funder and the Assignee fully and continually informed of all material developments in connection with the Arbitral Award and the Subject Claims, in each case in accordance with Sections 11.3 and 14.1 of the ICEA; 2 (C) Limited Direction of the Nominated Lawyers by the Funder . Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, the ICEA or the ORM Services Agreement, the Assignor hereby specifically authorizes and permits the Funder to direct the Nominated Lawyers to instruct, on the Assignor’s behalf, any party related in any way to the Claimholder Proceeds that any such Claimholder Proceeds be paid to the Escrow Account (unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Assignor, the Assignee, ExO and the Funder); provided , however , that the Funder, prior to so directing the Nominated Lawyers, gives notice to the Assignor of its intention to do so and affords the Assignor reasonable opportunity to discuss the advisability of doing so; (D) Power of Attorney . The Assignor irrevocably directs the Nominated Lawyers to take all steps necessary to ensure that any and all Claimholder Proceeds paid to Assignor are paid or delivered into the Escrow Account (or as otherwise agreed in writing by the Assignor, the Assignee, ExO and the Funder). The Assignor herein grants to the Nominated Lawyers a full and irrevocable power of attorney (or local law equivalent where any Proceeds are received) to collect and cause any and all Claimholder Proceeds to be paid into the Escrow Account (unless otherwise agreed in writing by the Assignor, the Assignee, ExO and the Funder); (E) Security . Assignor’s grant of a first-priority security interest in the Collateral pursuant to Section 8.1 of the ICEA remains in full force and effect. Assignor acknowledges the validity and enforceability of the UCC-1 Initial Financing Statement with the Nevada filing number F202604060243[, as it was amended by UCC-3 Amendment with the Nevada filing number [•]] (the “Assignor UCC Financing Statement”); (F) Obligations Unaffected by Insolvency . All of the ICEA Continuing Obligations of the Assignor, including this Agreement and any documents provided by way of security, are intended to survive the insolvency or liquidation of the Assignor, including any Insolvency Proceeding; (G) Access to Records . At the request of Assignee, the Funder, or any of their respective Affiliates, the Assignor shall provide reasonable access to Assignor’s records and personnel in connection with the maintenance, defense and enforcement of the Arbitral Award and any litigation relating to the Arbitral Award; (H) Claimholder Representative . The Assignor hereby designates John Longley to serve as its primary contact with respect to this Agreement and to act as its authorized representative with respect to matters pertaining to this Agreement (the “ Claimholder Representative ”), with such designation to remain in force unless and until a successor is appointed, in the Assignor’s reasonable discretion, and the Assignor notifies the Funder of such change in writing. The Claimholder Representative shall be responsible for all notices and reporting obligations under this Agreement. 3 (I) Duty to Cooperate . The Assignor shall pursue the Subject Claim in a commercially reasonable manner substantially similar to the manner in which it pursued the Subject Claim prior to the date of this Agreement, at Assignee’s expense. Subject to the terms of the ORM Services Agreement, the Assignor shall provide support and cooperation in connection, at the direction and expense of the Assignee, with the pursuit of the Subject Claim, consistent with the Arbitral Award Support Services. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the Assignor shall irrevocably instruct the Nominated Lawyers to keep the Assignee and the Funder reasonably informed of all material developments (including the matters set out below) and to provide the Assignee and the Funder with copies of all documents material to the Subject Claim. The Assignor shall provide at least one (1) Business Day’s prior written notice to Assignee of Assignor’s substantive calls and meetings with the Nominated Lawyers to the extent commercially practicable and Assignee shall be entitled to participate in all such calls and meetings. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Assignor, the Assignee and the Funder agree that the Nominated Lawyers may not disclose information or documents, and the Assignee may not participate in calls or meetings or portions thereof, that the Nominated Lawyers reasonably believe could or would jeopardize any privilege, including the attorney-client privilege, of the Assignor. Additionally, the Assignor shall, as requested by the Assignee or the Nominated Lawyers and subject to the terms of the ORM Services Agreement: (1) cooperate with the Nominated Lawyers and their designees, the Assignee and the Funder in all material matters pertaining to the Subject Claim and devote sufficient time and attention as is reasonably necessary to conclude the Subject Claim; provide to the Nominated Lawyers and their designees all material Documentation and Confidential Information and comply with this Agreement; consult with the Nominated Lawyers and their designees as they reasonably require for purposes of pursuing the Subject Claim and appear at any proceeding or hearings (including hearings located abroad) reasonably required in connection with the Subject Claim; (2) cause all Persons related to the Subject Claim, including the Assignor’s legal representatives, to (i) submit to examination by the Nominated Lawyers and their designees for the preparation of statements, to subscribe to the same under oath if required, (ii) consult with the Nominated Lawyers and their designees as they reasonably require for purposes of pursuing the Subject Claim, and (iii) appear at any hearings (including hearings located abroad) reasonably required in connection with such statements or the Subject Claim generally; 4 (3) lend its name to all required actions and steps in relation to the Subject Claim, and shall execute all papers and render assistance to the Nominated Lawyers and their designees so as to secure to the Assignee and the Funder the benefits, rights and causes of action provided for herein. The Assignor shall: (i) do nothing that is reasonably likely to prejudice such benefits, rights or causes of action, and (ii) engage in no conduct or commercial arrangements that are reasonably likely to have a material adverse impact in any way on the Subject Claim or the value of the Proceeds; and (4) authorize and instruct the Nominated Lawyers and their designees to respond fully and promptly to any reasonable request by the Assignee, the Funder or their representatives for information regarding the Subject Claim. The Parties acknowledge and agree that the Assignor’s obligation to cooperate as set out in this section is essential to this Agreement and is a condition thereof and a continuing obligation and that any uncured material breach thereof that has a material adverse impact on the value of the Subject Claim or the Proceeds shall entitle the Funder to seek damages and equitable relief (including specific performance); provided , that in no event shall any breach or termination of this Agreement give rise to any right of rescission of, or otherwise affect, the assignment and assumption set forth in Section 1 above or the release set forth in Section 2(a) below, each of which is irrevocable. (J) No Action Relating to Subject Claim . Neither the Assignor nor any of its representatives will (i) institute any action, suit, or arbitration separate from the Subject Claim arising from the same facts, circumstances or law giving rise to the Subject Claim without the Funder’s knowledge and consent, which consent may be withheld in Funder’s sole discretion; (ii) take any step reasonably likely to have a materially adverse impact on the Subject Claim or the Funder’s share of any Proceeds; or (iii) take any step reasonably likely to give any Person or entity an interest in the Subject Claim or potential Proceeds except as otherwise permitted by this Agreement. (K) Cooperation on Insurance Matters . The Parties shall cooperate with each other to obtain adverse costs, political risk or similar insurance, if deemed necessary and desirable in the reasonable discretion of the Funder, at no out-of-pocket cost to the Assignor. 5 (L) Restrictive Covenants . The Assignor shall not, and shall cause its representatives and Affiliates not to, (A) dispose of, transfer, assign, or cause or permit the imposition of any Encumbrance on any of its right, title or interest in or relating to the Subject Claims, the Proceeds, or its beneficial interest in the foregoing, in whole or in part; (B) take or omit to take any action that constitutes or would reasonably be expected to constitute a Subject Claim Impairment, including: (1) any transfer or arrangement that would reduce, impair or otherwise materially and prejudicially affect the Subject Claims or the Proceeds or any part thereof; (2) any set-off, counterclaim or cross-claim by any Person in respect of the Subject Claims or the Proceeds; or (3) any arrangement or agreement (written or oral) with any Person to grant a contingent interest in, or a right to payment determined by reference to, the Subject Claims or the Proceeds, except as otherwise expressly permitted under the ICEA. The Assignor shall promptly disclose to the Funder and the Assignee any actual or potential Subject Claim Impairment of which the Assignor or any of its representatives becomes aware. (M) Funding of Subject Claim . The Assignor shall have no obligation to provide funding in connection with or to incur any expense with respect to the Subject Claims. The Assignee shall provide funding to the Assignor and reimburse Assignor’s expenses in connection with the Subject Claim in accordance with the ORM Services Agreement and without the Funder’s consent. The Assignor shall not negotiate for or accept any third-party investment, financing or funding of any type (including debt, equity or otherwise), from whatever source, and whether or not in cash, in connection with the Subject Claim without the prior written consent of the Funder, which consent may be withheld in Funder’s sole discretion. 2. Consent of Funder; Management of Subject Claim; Subordination (a) Subject to the satisfaction (or waiver) of the conditions set forth in Section 4 , effective as of the Closing Date, the Funder hereby consents to this Agreement and to the assignment and assumption set forth herein. The Funder agrees that, on and after the Closing Date, (i) the Assignor shall have no obligations under the ICEA other than the ICEA Continuing Obligations, and (ii) the Funder hereby irrevocably releases, acquits, and forever discharges Assignor from its obligations under the ICEA (other than with respect to the ICEA Continuing Obligations). Such release and discharge, and the assignment and assumption set forth in Section 1 , are irrevocable and shall survive any termination of, or any breach or alleged breach of, this Agreement. (b) Notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein, the foregoing release shall not release, discharge, impair, or otherwise affect (i) any obligations of ExO under the ICEA or (ii) any obligations of Assignor pursuant to this Agreement or the ORM Services Agreement. The foregoing release shall similarly not be construed as a limitation on the Funder’s remedies under this Agreement or the ORM Services Agreement, including the right to indemnity pursuant to Section 6 hereof. (c) In conjunction with the assignment and assumption of the ICEA set forth herein, the Parties agree that: 6 (i) Funder’s Passive Role . The Funder is not, and does not by virtue of consenting to the assignment become, a party to the Subject Claim nor does the Funder have any rights as to the direction, control, settlement or other conduct of the Subject Claim except as expressly set forth in the ICEA and this Agreement. The Funder does not have any rights as to the direction, control or conduct of the Nominated Lawyers, other than as set forth in the ICEA and this Agreement; (ii) Common Purpose . The Parties acknowledge and mutually represent to each other that it is their common purpose to enable the Assignor to pursue the Subject Claim in accordance with the ICEA Continuing Obligations and the ORM Services Agreement. The Parties further agree that this common purpose and all steps and actions required to achieve this common purpose, including any and all steps and actions required pursuant to the ICEA Continuing Obligations, are of the essence of the Funder’s consent herein; (iii) Strategic Decisions . Subject to the terms of the ICEA, the Assignor shall have the right to control all strategic decisions, proceedings, and, if applicable, settlement relating to the Subject Claims and the Arbitral Award, including, without limitation, all interactions (including any litigation) with the Funder in respect of the Litigation Financing Obligations. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Assignor shall not, and shall cause each of its Affiliates not to, take any material action or make any material decision with respect to the Subject Claims (including any settlement thereof), the Arbitral Award (including any settlement thereof), or the Litigation Financing Obligations without the prior written consent of the Assignee, and the Assignee shall timely respond to any such request from the Assignor for the Assignee’s prior written consent. Assignor shall be entitled to seek written consent or instruction from the Assignee with respect to any decision or action relating to the Subject Claim and the Arbitral Award and shall be entitled to rely on any such written consent or instruction. (iv) Monetary Settlement of Subject Claim . The Parties acknowledge that their common interest is served by settling the Subject Claim for a commercially reasonable amount. The Assignor and the Assignee shall not agree to any settlement relating to the Subject Claims or the Arbitral Award without the prior written consent of the Funder; provided, however, that the Funder’s prior written consent shall not be required if the amount of any such settlement is in an amount equal to the full amount of the Arbitral Award plus all then accrued but unpaid interest thereon (x) as determined by final order of the Ontario court or other court of competent jurisdiction or (y) calculated based on a risk-free rate (determined as the U.S. Treasury 1-year rate) plus a country-risk premium for Mexico (determined as the Emerging Markets Bond Index (EMBI) spread for Mexico) as determined and calculated by Compass Lexecon or another expert (including a nationally recognized accounting firm) agreed by the Parties. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Assignee and Funder acknowledge that Section 6.3, Section 7.1(c) and Section 7.4 of the ICEA shall apply to any settlement of the Subject Claims or the Arbitral Award notwithstanding anything to the contrary contained herein or in the ORM Services Agreement. 7 (v) Follow-on Funding . Notwithstanding Section 5.7 of the ICEA, the Funder shall not have the option to continue funding the Fees and Expenses in relation to the Subject Claim unless the Assignee fails to fund such Fees and Expenses, in which case Funder shall have the option to continue funding the Fees and Expenses in relation to the Subject Claim on the same terms and conditions provided in the ICEA in accordance with Section 5.7 of the ICEA. Funder must exercise its option to continue funding in writing, within thirty (30) days after (1) notice by Funder to Assignee of Assignee’s failure to fund the Fees and Expenses and the expiration of a ten (10) day cure period, or (2) notice by Assignee to Funder of Assignee’s inability to fund the Fees and Expenses. (vi) Assignment of Arbitral Rights . The Assignor shall assign to Assignee, and Assignee shall assume, the Arbitral Rights, including any judgment in favor of Assignor in relation thereto (A) as promptly as reasonably practicable upon the written request of the Assignee at any time prior to entry of a final judgment with respect to the Arbitral Rights by a court of competent jurisdiction, or (B) as soon as practicable, but no later than ninety (90) days, following entry of a final judgment by a court of competent jurisdiction in favor of the Assignor or ExO against the United Mexican States enforceable in the United States or Canada with respect to the Arbitral Award. Notwithstanding the foregoing, no such assignment, transfer or other arrangement shall be made or required (1) to the extent such assignment is not permitted under applicable law, treaty or regulation, which permission under applicable law, treaty or regulation may be demonstrated by written approval by a competent Governmental Authority (including pursuant to a final order of a court of competent jurisdiction), (2) if it would reasonably be expected to impair enforcement of the Arbitral Award or such judgment or prejudice the rights or position of the Assignee or ExO as claimant or judgment creditor, or (3) solely with respect to an assignment in accordance with subsection (A), without the prior written consent of the Funder in form and substance satisfactory to the Assignor. Such assignment shall be made pursuant to a form of assignment and assumption agreement satisfactory to Assignor, Assignee and Funder, which assignment and assumption agreement shall provide for a full release and indemnity of Assignor by Assignee and Funder relating to the Arbitral Rights and the Subject Claim, including under the ORM Services Agreement. (vii) Security Interest . In conjunction with the security interest granted by Assignee pursuant to Section 8.1 of the ICEA, Assignee hereby authorizes the Funder to file a UCC-1 financing statement against Assignee with the same description of collateral as set forth in the Assignor UCC Financing Statement. Nothing in this Agreement or the Assignee’s assumption hereunder shall authorize or entitle the Funder to file a UCC-1 financing statement or similar public filing in any jurisdiction against Assignee or any of its Affiliates other than as described in this subsection without the Assignee’s prior written consent. Nothing in this Agreement or the Assignee’s assumption hereunder affects the validity or enforceability of (i) the UCC-1 Financing Statement filed against ExO in the District of Columbia with filing number 2026033139 and (ii) the RUG filing (Guarantee No. 8906111) and the related non-possessory pledge agreement ( prenda sin transmisión de posesión ) granted by ExO in favor of the Funder. 8 (d) The Funder agrees: (i) all amounts expended by Assignee, including but not limited to amounts payable under the ORM Services Agreement and expended for general corporate purposes consistent with the annual budget approved by Assignee’s board of directors, may benefit Funder by advancing enforcement and collection of the Arbitral Award or supporting efforts to settle the Subject Claim, which may result in Proceeds being paid to Funder or the Claims Payments being converted to a note payable to Funder by Assignee or ExO in accordance with the ICEA. As such, all amounts payable to Funder pursuant to the ICEA in respect of Proceeds will be subordinated to amounts payable to the PCM Purchasers (as defined below) in an amount, as of the date of payment, equal to the sum of (x) the excess, if any, of the aggregate purchase price paid by the PCM Purchasers for Series A Preferred Stock pursuant to the Subscription Agreements over the PCM Investments (as defined below), plus (y) the greater of (1) PCM Investments accreted at 20% per annum on a paid-in-kind basis, compounded annually, and (2) 150% of the PCM Investments. For purposes of this Agreement, (A) “ PCM Investments ” means all funding amounts expended by Assignee, whether for legal expenses to enforce the Arbitral Award as approved by Assignee’s board of directors (including legal expenses incurred by Assignor at the request of Assignee that are reimbursed under the ORM Services Agreement), general corporate purposes consistent with the annual budget approved by Assignee’s board of directors, or to support settlement discussions with respect to the Subject Claims or Arbitral Rights (such as development of the environmental permit filed by Phosagmex that is necessary for its project to move forward); and (B) “PCM Purchasers” means the purchasers of Series A preferred stock of Assignee in the initial funding of Assignee pursuant to the subscription agreements substantially in the form annexed hereto as Exhibit [B] (the “ Subscription Agreements ”); and (ii) In the event of any settlement of the Subject Claims or Arbitral Rights, as consideration for the amounts expended by Assignee and its Affiliates to achieve such settlement, which may benefit the Funder, Funder will not pursue against Assignee or any of its stockholders or Affiliates, other than ExO, a value of any Conversion Amount greater than 500% of the Claims Payments made by Funder. For the avoidance of doubt, nothing in this subsection (ii) constitutes an agreement or determination of the amount of any Proceeds that may be payable to Funder under the ICEA by Assignee or ExO. (iii) The provisions of this Section 2(d) shall be restated in the stockholders’ agreement to be entered into by Assignee, the PCM Purchasers and certain other parties in connection with the PCM Investments (the “ Stockholders’ Agreement ”). The PCM Purchasers are intended third-party beneficiaries of this Section 2(d) and shall be entitled to enforce the provisions hereof directly against the Funder. In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the provisions of this Section 2(d) and the corresponding provisions of the Stockholders’ Agreement, the Stockholders’ Agreement shall control. 3. Representations and Warranties (a) Each of the Parties represents and warrants to the other Parties as of the date of this Agreement that: (i) it is validly organized and existing and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its formation; (ii) it has all requisite corporate power and authority to conduct its business as it is presently conducted; (iii) it has taken all necessary action to authorize the creation, execution, delivery and performance of this Agreement, and this Agreement has been duly executed by such Party, as required, and when delivered will be a legal, valid and binding obligation of such Party, and enforceable in accordance with its terms; 9 (iv) the execution and delivery of and performance by it of this Agreement (A) does not and will not (or would not with the giving of notice, the lapse of time or the happening of any other event or condition) constitute or result in a violation or breach of, or conflict with, or allow any other person to exercise any rights under, any of the terms or provisions of its organizational documents or by-laws; (B) does not and will not (or would not with the giving of notice, the lapse of time or the happening of any other event or condition) constitute or result in a breach or violation of, or conflict with or allow any other person to exercise any rights under, any of the terms or provisions of any agreement to which it is a party; and (C) does not and will not result in the violation of any law. Each of the Parties acknowledges that the other Parties are relying on the foregoing representations and warranties in connection with entering into this Agreement in accordance with the terms hereof and that the representations and warranties set forth above shall survive the execution and delivery of this Agreement. (b) The Assignor represents and warrants to the Assignee and the Funder that, as of the Effective Date: (i) The Assignor and ExO are the sole legal and beneficial owners of, and have good title to, the Subject Claim, free and clear of any Encumbrances other than the security interests granted to the Funder pursuant to the ICEA; (ii) Neither the Assignor, ExO, nor, to the knowledge of the Assignor’s officers and directors, any of their representatives has: (A) taken any steps or executed any documents which would materially or adversely affect the Subject Claim; (B) engaged in any acts or conduct or made any material omissions, agreements or arrangements, that would result in the Funder receiving proportionately less payments or less favorable treatment in respect of the Subject Claim than the Assignor pursuing or enforcing such Subject Claim; (C) set-off or agreed to set-off any amounts against the Subject Claim or the Proceeds and no rights of set-off or similar rights against the Assignor exist which will permit any set-off of or counterclaim against the Subject Claim; (D) made or entered into any prior assignment, trust arrangement, security, sale, transfer or sub-participation or local law equivalent of its right, title or interest in the Subject Claim that remains in effect as of the date of this Agreement; or 10 (E) received any written notice or is otherwise aware that the Subject Claim or any portion thereof is subject to any Subject Claim Impairment or is otherwise invalid or void other than the application to set aside the Arbitral Award submitted by the United Mexican States that is pending as of the date of this Agreement; (iii) The Assignor has disclosed or caused to be disclosed to the Funder all material documentation and other information in its possession or control relevant to the Subject Claim, in its true, complete and correct form, and there is no information in the knowledge, possession or control of the Assignor or its legal representatives that is or is reasonably likely to be material to the Funder’s assessment of the Subject Claim that has not been disclosed to the Funder; (iv) No proceedings of or before any Governmental Authority, other than the application to set aside the Arbitral Award submitted by the United Mexican States that is pending as of the date of this Agreement, have been commenced by or against or, to the best of the Assignor’s or ExO’s knowledge, are threatened against the Assignor or ExO, which are reasonably likely to materially adversely affect the Subject Claim; and (v) The assignment and assumption of obligations pursuant to this Agreement will not adversely affect the Assignor’s legal right to continue to enforce the Arbitral Award. 4. Conditions to Effectiveness (a) The obligations of the Parties hereunder, including but not limited to the assignment and assumption set forth in Section 1 and the release set forth in Section 2(a) of this Agreement, are subject to the satisfaction, on or prior to the Closing Date, of each of the following conditions, unless waived in writing by each of the Parties: (i) the Pre-Closing Reorganization shall have been effected pursuant to the [Pre-Closing Reorganization Documents] 1 ; (ii) the Assignor and the Assignee shall have executed and delivered to the Funder the ORM Services Agreement; (iii) the Funder and the Assignor shall have executed the [Warrant Redemption Agreement]; (iv) the Subscription Agreements shall have been executed by the Assignee and the PCM Purchasers and all of the conditions to the purchase and sale of the Assignee’s preferred stock thereunder shall have been satisfied; and 1 NTD: To be defined to include the necessary contribution and distribution agreements, the trust agreement, and other reorganization documents. 11 (v) all conditions to the closing of the Merger shall have been satisfied or waived (other than the effectiveness of this Agreement and other than those conditions which, by their nature, are to be satisfied at the closing of the transactions contemplated by the Merger Agreement), and the Effective Time (as defined in the Merger Agreement) shall be set to occur substantially concurrently with the effectiveness hereof. 5. Confidentiality; Common Interest Section 2(d) ( Common Interest ) and Section 13 ( Confidentiality ) of the ORM Services Agreement are incorporated herein by reference and shall apply to the Parties under this Agreement mutatis mutandis . 6. Indemnification (a) Indemnification by the Assignee . The Assignee agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Assignor and its stockholders, officers, directors, employees, agents and other representatives and its and their respective successors and assigns (the “ Assignor Indemnified Parties ”) for, from and against any and all losses, damages, liabilities, costs and expenses (including reasonable legal, accounting and other costs and expenses of professionals), interest, awards, judgments and penalties (hereinafter, “ Losses ”) actually suffered or incurred by them, directly or indirectly, arising out of or resulting from (i) any material breach by the Assignee or its representatives of any provision of this Agreement, (ii) the Assignee’s or its representatives’ fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct in connection with Assignee’s obligations under this Agreement or the ICEA, (iii) the Litigation Financing Obligations (other than the ICEA Continuing Obligations), or (iv) any written instruction of the Assignee or failure to provide timely consent pursuant to Section 2(c)(iii) of this Agreement, in each case of the foregoing clauses (i) through (iv), except to the extent directly or indirectly arising out of or resulting from the fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct by the Assignor or its representatives. (b) Indemnification by the Assignor . The Assignor agrees to indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Assignee and its stockholders, officers, directors, employees, agents and other representatives and its and their respective successors and assigns (the “ Assignee Indemnified Parties”) and the Funder, its respective stockholders, members, partners, equityholders, agents and other representatives and its and their respective successors and assigns (the “ Funder Indemnified Parties ” and, together with the Assignor Indemnified Parties and the Assignee Indemnified Parties, the “ Indemnified Parties ”) for, from and against any and all Losses actually suffered or incurred by them, directly or indirectly, arising out of or resulting from any material breach of this Agreement by the Assignor or its representatives, except to the extent directly or indirectly arising out of or resulting from the fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct of the Assignee or the Funder or their respective representatives, written instruction of the Assignee or Funder, or the Assignee’s or Funder’s failure to provide timely consent pursuant to Section 2(c)(iii) of this Agreement. Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the aggregate liability of the Assignor pursuant to this Section 6 shall not exceed the amount of the Arbitral Award plus interest accrued as of the date of determination, as calculated in accordance with Section 2 ; provided , however , that the foregoing limitation shall not apply in the event the Losses arise as a result of Assignor’s or its representatives’ fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct. 12 (c) An Indemnified Party shall give the applicable indemnifying party (the “ Indemnifying Party ”) written notice in reasonable detail of any matter which such Indemnified Party has determined has given or is reasonably likely to give rise to a right of indemnification under this Agreement, within thirty (30) days of such determination, including all material facts and circumstances that give rise to such right of indemnification, the amount of the Loss, if known, and the method of computation thereof, and containing a reference to the provisions of this Agreement in respect of which such right of indemnification is claimed or arises; provided , however , that the failure to provide such notice shall not release the Indemnifying Party from any of its obligations under this Section 6 . (d) The Indemnifying Party shall respond to any such notice within thirty (30) days of receipt thereof, specifying in reasonable detail whether it disputes all or any portion of the right to indemnification claimed therein (the “ Response Period ”). If the Indemnifying Party does not respond within the Response Period, the Indemnifying Party shall be deemed to have accepted liability for the full amount of the Loss as set forth in such notice. If the Indemnifying Party timely disputes its obligation to indemnify, in whole or in part, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to resolve such dispute for a period of thirty (30) days following delivery of the Indemnifying Party’s response, and any dispute not resolved during such period shall be submitted for resolution in accordance with Section 11 of this Agreement. (e) If an Indemnified Party shall receive notice of any action, audit, claim, mediation, demand, assessment, suit, arbitration, litigation, hearing, proceeding, formal inquiry, formal investigation or similar proceeding by or before any Governmental Authority or brought by any third-party against the Indemnified Party (each, a “ Third-Party Claim ”, and each such proceeding, an “ Action ”) which may give rise to a claim for Loss under this Section 6 , within thirty (30) days of the receipt of such notice, the Indemnified Party shall give the Indemnifying Party written notice of such Third-Party Claim; provided , however , that the failure to provide such notice shall not release the Indemnifying Party from any of its obligations under this Section 6 . The Indemnifying Party shall be entitled to assume and control the defense of such Third-Party Claim at its expense and through counsel of its choice if it gives written notice of its intention to do so to the Indemnified Party within forty-five (45) days of the receipt of such notice from the Indemnified Party; provided that the Indemnifying Party shall not have the right to assume and control the defense of any Third-Party Claim that (i) seeks an injunction or other equitable relief against the Indemnified Party that cannot reasonably be separated from any related claim for money damages, or (ii) is a criminal Action. (f) If the Indemnifying Party elects to assume the defense of a Third-Party Claim: (A) the Indemnified Party may participate in such defense at its own expense, subject to the Indemnifying Party’s right to control the defense thereof; (B) the Indemnified Party shall cooperate with the Indemnifying Party in such defense and make available to the Indemnifying Party, at the Indemnifying Party’s expense, all witnesses, pertinent records, materials and information in the Indemnified Party’s possession or under the Indemnified Party’s control relating thereto as is reasonably required by the Indemnifying Party; (C) the Indemnifying Party shall not, without the prior written consent of the Indemnified Party, enter into any settlement or compromise or consent to the entry of any judgment with respect to such Third-Party Claim if such settlement, compromise or judgment (1) involves a finding or admission of wrongdoing by the Indemnified Party or any of its Affiliates, (2) does not include an unconditional written release by the claimant or plaintiff of the Indemnified Party and its Affiliates from all liability in respect of such Third-Party Claim, or (3) imposes equitable remedies or any obligation on the Indemnified Party or any of its Affiliates 13 other than solely the payment of money damages for which the Indemnified Party will be indemnified hereunder; and (D) the Indemnified Party shall not pay, or permit to be paid, any part of such Third-Party Claim unless the Indemnifying Party consents in writing to such payment or unless the Indemnifying Party withdraws from the defense of such Third-Party Claim or unless a final judgment from which no appeal may be taken by or on behalf of the Indemnifying Party is entered against the Indemnified Party for such Third-Party Claim. (g) Notwithstanding the foregoing, if (A) a conflict of interest exists between the Indemnifying Party and the Indemnified Party with respect to such Third-Party Claim, or (B) the Indemnifying Party fails to actively and diligently prosecute the defense of such Third-Party Claim, the Indemnified Party shall have the right to engage separate counsel of its own choosing at the Indemnifying Party’s expense, and the Indemnifying Party shall reimburse the Indemnified Party for the reasonable and documented out-of-pocket fees and expenses of such separate counsel promptly upon demand. (h) If the Indemnifying Party does not (or does not have the right to) assume the defense of any Third-Party Claim pursuant to Section 6(e) , the Indemnified Party shall undertake the defense of such Third-Party Claim and may propose to compromise or otherwise settle such Third-Party Claim prior to a final judgment thereon or to forgo any appeal with respect thereto, provided that the Indemnified Party shall give the Indemnifying Party prompt written notice thereof, provided further that the Indemnified Party shall not admit any liability with respect to, or settle, compromise or discharge any Third-Party Claim without the Indemnifying Party’s prior written consent (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed). (i) Each Indemnified Party shall, and shall cause its representatives to, take commercially reasonable steps to mitigate any Loss in respect of which it is or may be entitled to indemnification under this Section 6, including availing itself of any defenses, limitations, rights of contribution, and claims against third-parties that are reasonably available to it; provided, however, that nothing in this Section 6(i) shall require any Indemnified Party to take any action that would be unreasonably burdensome, that would materially and adversely affect such Indemnified Party’s business operations or legal rights, or that would require such Indemnified Party to waive, compromise or prejudice any right or remedy available to it under this Agreement or otherwise. 7. Limitation of Liability (a) No Party or any of its representatives shall be liable to any other Party or such other Party’s representatives with respect to this Agreement, whether in contract, tort (including negligence and strict liability) or otherwise, including with respect to any indemnification obligation set forth in Section 6 ( Indemnification ), for any punitive, incidental, consequential, special or indirect damages, including loss of future profits, revenue or income, diminution in value or loss of business reputation or opportunity or exemplary damages (except to the extent any such damages are paid by a Party or its Affiliates to a third-party pursuant to a final non-appealable judgment or settlement in connection with the final determination or settlement of a Third-Party Claim); provided , however , except with respect to punitive damages, the foregoing shall not limit the Assignor’s liability arising out of or resulting from a material breach of this Agreement, a material breach of the ORM Services Agreement with respect to the Arbitral Award Support 14 Services, or any fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct in connection with an action taken or omission with respect to the Arbitral Award, the Subject Claims or the Arbitral Rights that results in a material reduction of the amount of the Arbitral Award or materially adversely affects the collectability of the Arbitral Award, unless any such action or omission is at the written instruction of or due to the failure of the Assignee or Funder to provide its timely consent. (b) The foregoing limitation of liability provision shall not apply in the event of a Party’s or a Party’s representatives’ fraud, gross negligence or willful misconduct. (c) The indemnification and remedies in Section 6 ( Indemnification ) and this Section 7 ( Limitation of Liability ), together with any other remedy which is expressly provided for in this Agreement shall be the exclusive remedies of the Parties with respect to the subject matter of this Agreement. 8. Amendments (a) This Agreement may not be amended except in writing signed by each of the Parties. (b) The ICEA may not be amended in any manner that affects the Assignor without the prior written consent of the Assignor. (c) The Assignor and Assignee may not amend Section 2(a)(ii) of the ORM Services Agreement without the prior written consent of the Funder. 9. Binding Nature; Assignment This Agreement is effective on the Effective Date. From and after the Effective Date, this Agreement will be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Parties and their respective successors. No Party shall have the right to sell, assign or transfer any part or parts of this Agreement, except that any Party may assign this Agreement to a successor to all or substantially all of its business or assets (whether by merger, consolidation, operation of law or otherwise); provided , that no such assignment shall relieve the assigning Party of its obligations hereunder. Any permitted assignment under this Section 9 shall be conditioned upon the assignee expressly assuming and agreeing in writing to be bound by all of the terms and conditions of this Agreement. In the case of any merger, consolidation or similar transaction involving the Assignor, the successor or surviving entity shall, by operation of such transaction, be bound by all of the Assignor’s obligations hereunder, and the Assignor shall cause such successor or surviving entity to expressly confirm in writing its assumption of such obligations. Any attempted assignment in violation of this Section 9 shall be void ab initio . 10. Governing Law This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the Laws of the State of New York (without regard to any conflict of Laws or choice of Laws rules or principles that would cause or permit the application of the Laws of any other jurisdiction) as to all matters, including matters of validity, construction, effect, performance and remedies. 15 11. Dispute Resolution (a) Prior to commencing any arbitration under this Section 11 , the Parties shall submit any dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement to a senior executive officer designated in writing by each Party for resolution. If such officers fail to resolve the dispute within thirty (30) days following its submission to them, the dispute shall be resolved by arbitration in accordance with this Section 11 . (b) Any dispute between the Parties arising out of or relating to the interpretation or performance of this Agreement that is not resolved as provided in Section 11(a) shall be finally resolved by arbitration administered by JAMS in accordance with its Expedited Procedures and subject to its Comprehensive Arbitration Rules and Procedures (the “ Rules ”). (c) The number of arbitrators shall be three (3). The claimant Party or Parties shall jointly appoint one (1) arbitrator, the respondent Party or Parties shall jointly appoint one (1) arbitrator, and the third arbitrator, who shall serve as chair, shall be appointed by the two (2) Party-appointed arbitrators. If, within thirty (30) calendar days after the appointment of the second arbitrator, the two (2) Party-appointed arbitrators have not appointed the third arbitrator, or if either side fails to appoint its arbitrator, such arbitrator shall be appointed by JAMS in accordance with the Rules. The place of arbitration shall be New York City. (d) The award of the arbitrators shall be final, non-appealable and binding on the Parties and may be presented by any Party for enforcement in any court of competent jurisdiction, and the Parties hereby consent to the jurisdiction of such court solely for purposes of enforcement of this arbitration agreement and any award rendered hereunder. In any such enforcement action, irrespective of where it is brought, no Party will seek to invalidate or modify the award of the arbitrators or otherwise to invalidate or circumvent the procedures set forth in this Section 11 . The fees of the arbitrators and the other costs of such arbitration shall be borne by the Parties as decided by the arbitrators and as set forth in the arbitration award. (e) Each of the Parties hereby irrevocably agrees not to claim and irrevocably waives any claim or right (whether claimed or not claimed) that it has or may hereafter acquire under any law or regulation to immunity for itself, or any of its revenues, assets or properties or those of any of its agencies, societies or other instrumentalities from the jurisdiction of any court with respect to the enforcement of or liability for any arbitral award or order of any court rendered pursuant to this Section 11 . (f) Nothing in this Section 11 shall be construed to preclude any Party from seeking provisional remedies, including, but not limited to, temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions, from any court of competent jurisdiction, in order to protect its rights prior to, or during the pendency of, the dispute resolution processes specified in this Section 11 . (g) The Parties acknowledge that the ORM Services Agreement contains a substantially similar agreement to arbitrate disputes before JAMS. To the extent that a dispute arising out of or relating to this Agreement and a dispute arising out of or relating to the ORM Services Agreement are pending concurrently and arise out of the same or a related set of facts, circumstances or transactions, such disputes shall be joined and consolidated and heard together 16 before a single arbitral tribunal. The tribunal constituted in the first-filed of such arbitrations shall have authority to determine any dispute regarding joinder or consolidation, and upon consolidation the consolidated proceeding shall be conducted before that tribunal. Each Party hereby consents to such joinder and consolidation and waives any objection thereto, including any objection based on the presence of additional or different parties in the consolidated proceeding. 12. Entire Agreement This Agreement constitutes the entire agreement of the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements and undertakings, both written and oral, among the Parties with respect to the subject matter herein. 13. Severability If any term or other provision of this Agreement is invalid, illegal or incapable of being enforced by any Law or public policy, all other terms and provisions of this Agreement shall nevertheless remain in full force and effect for so long as the economic or legal substance of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement is not affected in any manner materially adverse to any Party. Upon such determination by a court or arbitrator that any term or other provision is invalid, illegal or incapable of being enforced, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to modify this Agreement so as to effect the original intent of the Parties as closely as possible in an acceptable manner in order that the transactions contemplated by this Agreement are consummated as originally contemplated to the greatest extent possible. 14. No Waiver The failure of any Party to insist upon strict adherence to any provision of this Agreement on any occasion shall not be considered a waiver or deprive that Party of the right thereafter to insist upon strict adherence to such provision or any other provision of this Agreement. No purported waiver shall be effective as against any Party unless consented to in writing by such Party. The waiver by any Party of a breach of any provision of this Agreement shall not operate or be construed as a waiver of any subsequent or other breach. 15. Counterparts This Agreement may be executed and delivered (including by facsimile or other means of electronic transmission, such as by electronic mail in “pdf” form) in counterparts, each of which when executed shall be deemed to be an original, but all of which taken together shall constitute one and the same agreement. text: EX-10.8 9 d191731dex108.htm EX-10.8 EX-10.8 Exhibit 10.8 WARRANT REDEMPTION AGREEMENT This Warrant Redemption Agreement (this “ Agreement ”), dated as of [•], 2026, is entered into by and among Odyssey Marine Exploration, Inc. , a Nevada corporation (“ Odyssey ”), and Drumcliffe, LLC , a Delaware limited liability company (“ Drumcliffe ”). Odyssey and Drumcliffe are sometimes collectively referred to as the “ Parties .” All capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in this Agreement have the meanings given to them in the Warrant (as defined below). Recitals: A. Odyssey issued to Drumcliffe a Warrant to Purchase Common Stock, dated as of January 31, 2020 (the “ Warrant ”), exercisable to purchase the Exercise Shares ( i.e. , 551,378 shares of Common Stock) at the Exercise Price. B. Drumcliffe wishes to sell to Odyssey, and Odyssey wishes to purchase and redeem from Drumcliffe, the Warrant and all of Drumcliffe’s right, title, and interest in the Warrant, on the terms and subject to the conditions set forth in this Agreement. NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements hereinafter set forth and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows: Section 1. Redemption of Warrant. Subject to the terms and conditions set forth in this Agreement, at the Closing (as defined below), Drumcliffe shall sell, transfer, and deliver to Odyssey, and Odyssey shall purchase and redeem from Drumcliffe, all of Drumcliffe’s rights, title, and interest in and to the Warrant, free and clear of any pledge, lien, charge, security interest, mortgage, claim, or other encumbrance (each, an “ Encumbrance ”). Upon payment of the Purchase Price (as defined below) at the Closing, Drumcliffe shall cease to have any rights as a holder of the Warrant. Section 2. Purchase Price. The aggregate purchase price for the Warrant shall be $500,000.00 (the “ Purchase Price ”). Section 3. Payment Terms. Odyssey shall pay the Purchase Price to Drumcliffe at the Closing in cash or by wire transfer of immediately available funds to the account designated in Appendix A. Section 4. Closing. The closing of the transactions contemplated by this Agreement shall take place remotely by exchange of documents and signatures (or their electronic counterparts) (the “ Closing ”) as soon as practicable (and in any event within two business days) after the Effective Time (as defined in the Merger Agreement (as defined below)). As used in this Agreement, the “ Merger Agreement ” means the Agreement and Plan of Merger, dated as of April 8, 2026, as amended, among Odyssey, Oceanus Merger Sub, Inc., a Delaware corporation and a wholly owned subsidiary of Odyssey, and American Ocean Minerals Corporation. Section 5. Closing Deliverables. At the Closing, (a) Drumcliffe shall deliver to Odyssey an affidavit of lost warrant in the form attached as Appendix B in lieu of the original Warrant, and (b) Odyssey shall deliver to Drumcliffe the full Purchase Price in accordance with Section 3. Section 6. Representations and Warranties of Drumcliffe. Drumcliffe represents and warrants to Odyssey that: (a) Drumcliffe is the sole legal and beneficial owner of the Warrant, and such ownership is free and clear of all Encumbrances. (b) Drumcliffe has full power and authority to enter into this Agreement and the documents to be delivered by Drumcliffe hereunder and to consummate the transactions provided hereunder. The execution and delivery by Drumcliffe of this Agreement and performance by Drumcliffe of its obligations hereunder have been duly authorized by all necessary company action on the part of Drumcliffe. This Agreement has been duly executed and delivered to Odyssey by Drumcliffe and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of Drumcliffe, enforceable against Drumcliffe in accordance with its terms, except as may be limited by bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and other similar laws of general applicability relating to or affecting creditors’ rights or general equity principles (regardless of whether considered at law or in equity); (c) None of the execution, delivery, or performance by Drumcliffe, nor the consummation of the transaction contemplated hereby by Drumcliffe, will conflict with, result in the breach of, constitute a default under, or accelerate the performance required by the terms of: (i) any applicable law; (ii) the provisions of any material contract or agreement to which Drumcliffe is a party or to which any of Drumcliffe’s material assets are bound; or (iii) any of Drumcliffe’s organizational documents (including its articles or certificate of organization or formation or operating or limited liability company agreement. (d) Drumcliffe has not delivered any Notice of Exercise to Odyssey or otherwise exercised the Warrant in whole or in part. (e) By reason of Drumcliffe’s business or financial experience (either alone or together with its advisers), Drumcliffe has the capacity to protect its own interests in connection with the sale of the Warrant to Odyssey and to evaluate the potential risks and benefits of the sale hereunder of the Warrant. (f) Drumcliffe has received all of the information that Drumcliffe considers necessary or appropriate for deciding whether to sell the Warrant hereunder and perform the other transactions contemplated hereby. Drumcliffe further represents that Drumcliffe has had an opportunity to ask questions and receive answers from Odyssey regarding the business, properties, prospects, and financial condition of Odyssey and its subsidiaries and to seek from Odyssey such additional information as Drumcliffe has deemed necessary to verify the accuracy of any such information furnished or otherwise made available to Drumcliffe by or on behalf of Odyssey. Section 7. Representations and Warranties of Odyssey. Odyssey represents and warrants to Drumcliffe that: (a) The execution and delivery by Odyssey of this Agreement and performance by Odyssey of its obligations hereunder have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate action on the part of Odyssey. This Agreement has been duly executed and delivered by Odyssey and constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of Odyssey, enforceable against Odyssey in accordance with its terms, except as may be limited by bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and other similar laws of general applicability relating to or affecting creditors’ rights or general equity principles (regardless of whether considered at law or in equity); 2 (b) None of the execution, delivery, or performance by Odyssey, nor the consummation of the transaction contemplated hereby by Odyssey will conflict with, result in the breach of, constitute a default under or accelerate the performance required by the terms of: (i) any applicable law; (ii) the provisions of any material contract or agreement to which Odyssey is a party or to which any of Odyssey’s material assets are bound; or (iii) any of Odyssey’s organizational documents, including its articles of incorporation and bylaws, in each case as amended or restated. Section 8. Release. (a) Release by Drumcliffe. In consideration of the covenants, agreements, and undertakings of Odyssey set forth herein, effective upon the Closing, Drumcliffe, on behalf of itself, each of its affiliates, and each of their respective members, shareholders, partners, managers, directors, officers, employees, agents, and representatives, and successors and assigns of any of the foregoing (collectively, the “ Drumcliffe Releasing Parties ”), hereby absolutely, unconditionally, and irrevocably releases and discharges Odyssey, each of its affiliates, and each of their respective past, present, and future members, shareholders, partners, managers, directors, officers, employees, agents, and representatives, and successors and assigns of any of the foregoing (collectively, the “ Odyssey Released Parties ”) from any and all claims, counterclaims, actions, causes of action, suits, defenses, debts, obligations, promises, expenses, liabilities, setoffs, accounts, covenants, contracts, agreements, costs, judgments, and demands whatsoever, whether at law, in equity, contract, tort, or otherwise (whether fixed or contingent, known or unknown, liquidated, or unliquidated) (each, a “ Claim ”), which any of the Drumcliffe Releasing Parties ever had, now have, or may hereafter have, against any of the Odyssey Released Parties, arising out of or relating to the Warrants (collectively, the “ Drumcliffe Released Claims ”); provided, however , that the Drumcliffe Released Claims shall not include any rights and remedies of any Drumcliffe Releasing Party under or for breach of this Agreement. Each of the Drumcliffe Releasing Parties shall refrain from, directly or indirectly, asserting any Drumcliffe Released Claim or commencing, instituting, or causing to be commenced, any action of any kind against any Odyssey Released Party based upon or with respect to any Drumcliffe Released Claim. In entering into this release, Drumcliffe acknowledges and agrees, on behalf of itself and each Drumcliffe Releasing Party, that Claims or facts in addition to or different from what they now know, believe, or suspect to exist might hereafter be discovered; nevertheless, it is its intention by entering into this Agreement to fully, finally, and forever release, discharge, and settle all of the Drumcliffe Released Claims, notwithstanding the existence or possible future discovery of any such additional or different Claim or fact, and the existence or possible future discovery of any such additional or different Claim or fact will in no manner affect this Agreement or the release set forth herein. (b) Third-Party Beneficiaries. Each Company Released Party and each Drumcliffe Released Party that is not a Party shall be a third-party beneficiary of this Section 8. Section 9. Termination. Either Odyssey or Drumcliffe may terminate this Agreement upon notice to the other Party or Parties if the Effective Time has not occurred on or before the Outside Date (as defined in the Merger Agreement). In the event of the termination of this Agreement in accordance with this Section 9, this Agreement shall forthwith become void, and there shall be no liability on the part of any Party. 3 Section 10. Miscellaneous. (a) Governing Law. This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the internal laws of the State of Florida without giving effect to any choice or conflict of law provision or rule (whether of the State of Florida or any other jurisdiction) that would cause the application of laws of any jurisdiction other than those of the State of Florida. (b) Further Assurances. Each of the Parties shall execute and deliver such additional documents, instruments, conveyances, and assurances and take such further action as may be reasonably required to effectuate the transactions contemplated by this Agreement. (c) Survival of Representations and Warranties. The representations and warranties contained herein or made in writing by the Parties shall survive the Closing. (d) Expenses. All costs and expenses incurred in connection with this Agreement and the transactions contemplated hereby shall be paid by the Party incurring such costs and expenses. (e) Notices. All notices, requests, consents, claims, demands, waivers, and other communications hereunder shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been given (a) when delivered by hand (with written confirmation of receipt); (b) when received by the addressee if sent by a nationally recognized overnight courier (receipt requested); or (c) on the date sent by email of a PDF document (with confirmation of transmission) if sent during normal business hours of the recipient, and on the next business day if sent after normal business hours of the recipient. Such communications must be sent to the respective Party at the following address (or at such other address for a Party as shall be specified in a notice given in accordance with this Section 10(c): If to Odyssey: Odyssey Marine Exploration, Inc. 205 S. Hoover Boulevard Suite 210 Tampa, Florida 33609 Attention: Legal Department legal@odysseymarine.com If to Drumcliffe: Drumcliffe LLC 1209 N. Orange St. Wilmington, DE 19801 Attention: James C. Little (f) Interpretation; Headings. This Agreement shall be construed without regard to any presumption or rule requiring construction or interpretation against the Party drafting an instrument or causing any instrument to be drafted. The headings in this Agreement are for reference only and shall not by themselves affect the interpretation of this Agreement. (g) Severability. The invalidity or unenforceability of any provision of this Agreement shall not affect the validity or enforceability of any other provision of this Agreement, and each provision of this Agreement shall be severable and enforceable to the extent permitted by law. (h) Entire Agreement. This Agreement and the documents to be delivered hereunder constitute the sole and entire agreement of the Parties with respect to the subject matter contained herein and therein, and supersede all prior and contemporaneous understandings and agreements, both written and oral, with respect to such subject matter. 4 (i) Successors and Assigns. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the heirs, legal representatives, successors, and permitted assigns of the Parties. (j) Amendments; Waiver. No supplement, modification, or amendment of this Agreement shall be binding unless executed in writing by each of the Parties. No waiver of any of the provisions of this Agreement shall be binding unless in the form of a writing signed by the Party against whom enforcement of the waiver is sought, and no such waiver shall operate as a waiver of any other provisions hereof (whether or not similar), nor shall such waiver constitute a continuing waiver. Except as specifically provided herein, no failure to exercise or any delay in exercising any right or remedy hereunder shall constitute a waiver thereof. (k) Waiver of Jury Trial. Each Party acknowledges and agrees that any controversy which may arise under this Agreement is likely to involve complicated and difficult issues and, therefore, such Party irrevocably and unconditionally waives any right it may have to a trial by jury in respect of any legal action arising out of or relating to this Agreement or the transactions contemplated hereby. (l) Counterparts and Electronic Delivery. This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. This Agreement may be executed and delivered by electronic signature (including signatures provided through DocuSign, Adobe Sign, or any other platform or method that complies with the U.S. federal ESIGN Act of 2000, the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act, or any other applicable law, including any successor statute or analogous foreign legislation) and transmitted by any electronic means, including email, cloud-based signing platforms, or secure file-sharing services. An electronic signature shall have the same legal effect, validity, and enforceability as a manually executed original signature. Each party waives any right to raise as a defense or objection to the validity or enforceability of this Agreement that it was executed or delivered in electronic form.
